rows.statement: Extracts A10 from Audi's internalism/externalism distinction: internal assurance (can the agent explain why it reached this conclusion) and external assurance (does the mechanism actually produce reliable results) are separate, since an AI can give an excellent explanation while wrong and a deterministic verifier can be reliable without human-style explanation -- yielding a four-term non-collapse chain Explainability != Reliability != Correctness != Knowledge as an AI Engineering Platform principle.

rows.anchor: intellectual rigor; clarity; logical ability; reliable epistemic powers; appropriate conviction; intellectual courage. ... Agent epistemic profile: reliability, evidence discipline, contradiction sensitivity, uncertainty calibration, reasoning transparency, source discipline, revision behavior, resistance to unsupported assertions. ... could inform Agent Qualification / Agent Trust Profiles.
rows.statement: Translates Audi's virtue-epistemology traits (intellectual rigor, clarity, logical ability, reliable epistemic powers, appropriate conviction, intellectual courage) into a candidate 8-dimension 'Agent epistemic profile' (reliability, evidence discipline, contradiction sensitivity, uncertainty calibration, reasoning transparency, source discipline, revision behavior, resistance to unsupported assertions) proposed to inform a future Agent Qualification / Agent Trust Profile mechanism, explicitly not to be called 'virtues' in platform vocabulary.

rows.anchor: KNOW: 'Component A calls Component B.' UNDERSTAND: 'Component A calls Component B because B owns capability X under these constraints.' ... Knowledge + Relations + Explanation + Structure -> Understanding. I would not formalize this yet, but I would definitely preserve it as a research direction.
rows.statement: Proposes a Knowledge-vs-Understanding distinction (worked example: knowing 'A calls B' vs understanding 'A calls B because B owns capability X under these constraints'), sketched as Knowledge+Relations+Explanation+Structure->Understanding, explicitly deferred as a preserved future research direction rather than formalized now.

rows.anchor: Audi gives us: How knowledge is constructed ... Williamson gives us: How far the knowledge claim can legitimately extend ... KNOWLEDGEOS EPISTEMIC MODEL: AUDI (Grounding, Sources, Inference, Coherence, Testimony) | WILLIAMSON (Robustness, Limits, Defeat, Uncertainty, Higher-order) | GOVERNANCE (Authority, Acceptance, Scope, Lifecycle, Supersession)
rows.statement: Combines the Audi extraction ('how knowledge is constructed': source->grounding->evidence->inference->coherence->knowledge) with the Williamson extraction ('how far a knowledge claim can legitimately extend': knowledge->truth->robustness->margin-for-error->temporal-stability->higher-order-limits->unknowability) and a Governance dimension (authority/acceptance/scope/lifecycle/supersession) into one composite three-pillar KnowledgeOS Epistemic Model, with the explicit design rule that no arrow in the model may be implicit.
invariants: no arrow in the epistemic model may be implicit

lineage_claims.quote: And I would combine these with Williamson

rows.anchor: The research does not justify making KnowledgeOS a Bayesian engine, statistical engine, semantic engine, reasoning engine, knowledge graph, or 'epistemic operating system' in the broad sense. ... KnowledgeOS is a constitutional epistemic domain boundary that preserves the integrity of claims, evidence, justification, authority, epistemic standing, identity, uncertainty, conflict and historical revision, while interpretation, inference, prediction, search, normalization and semantic generation remain replaceable mechanisms outside the core.
rows.statement: Executive architectural decision narrowing the scope of KnowledgeOS to a constitutional epistemic domain boundary rather than any of the broader engine/OS framings proposed across the preceding book-extraction files; explicitly instructs 'do not implement the earlier God KnowledgeAggregate literally.'

lineage_claims.target: an earlier candidate 'God KnowledgeAggregate' from prior research
lineage_claims.quote: The most important DDD conclusion is equally important: Do not implement the earlier "God KnowledgeAggregate" literally.

rows.anchor: WORLD/SOURCES -> OBSERVATION/EVIDENCE -> INTERPRETATION/MODEL/HYPOTHESIS -> CLAIM/ASSERTION -> JUSTIFICATION/ASSESSMENT -> EPISTEMIC STANDING -> DECISION/ACTION ... Do not collapse the layers merely because a mechanism can produce all of them.
rows.statement: Identifies the strongest cross-book convergence as a seven-layer disciplined separation, with the rule that layers must not be collapsed merely because a single mechanism (e.g. an LLM) is technically capable of producing outputs at every layer.
invariants: Do not collapse the layers merely because a mechanism can produce all of them.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS should not try to produce truth. It should preserve the conditions under which claims can be responsibly admitted, assessed, revised, challenged, contextualized and acted upon. ... KnowledgeOS is the boundary that makes cognition governable.
rows.statement: Final position/verdict: the synthesis of Williamson+Chivers+Freedman+Stigler produces one architectural idea -- KnowledgeOS is a small, deterministic, constitutional consistency boundary (protecting identity, evidence relationship, epistemic standing, authority relationship, revision, conflict, uncertainty, history) surrounded by replaceable epistemic mechanisms (interpretation, reasoning, prediction, causal analysis, statistical analysis, search, experiment design, semantic normalization, AI generation, projection) that together enable governable cognition and decision, not truth production.

rows.anchor: Only Evidence and Provenance survive both lists.
rows.statement: Two Phase 1 Kernel member-list proposals 36 minutes apart (20:32 and 21:08, 2026-08-21): Document A — kernel as 'a deterministic runtime for governed knowledge state, authority, evidence, lifecycle and provenance' (members: authority mechanics, generic evidence mechanics, lifecycle, provenance); Document B — kernel as 'observation/evaluation mechanics with rules pushed out to a port' (members: Observation, Evidence, Rule evaluation protocol, Assessment, Result, Provenance). Only Evidence and Provenance appear in both; Authority and Lifecycle are in A only, Observation/Assessment/Result/Rule-evaluation are in B only. B is a self-declared revision of A after consulting an older baseline document, not an independent arrival. Caution recorded: the {Evidence, Provenance} intersection is a historical fact about two proposals, not a minimality result or a finding about the Kernel.

lineage_claims.quote: This older baseline materially changes the picture, and I would revise my previous integration assessment

rows.anchor: Weak Analogy Areas" because "Knowledge systems lack: deterministic execution
rows.statement: Material contradiction (candidate): Position A (20260821-2032, P1, 20:32) claims the kernel is 'closer to: a deterministic runtime for governed knowledge state, authority, evidence, lifecycle and provenance'; Position B (20260821-2351, P2, 23:51, same evening, 3h19m later) rates the Unix/Linux analogy as weak because 'knowledge systems lack: deterministic execution, strict process isolation, universal semantics.' A possible reconciliation (governance-determinism vs. execution-determinism) is explicitly NOT accepted since neither document draws the distinction; v1.1's silence on determinism leaves workbook item W:C-2 (determinism: property, test, or DEF-1?) open and unruled.
missing: a corpus-internal resolution of the determinism contradiction

rows.anchor: the intersection of the two earliest Phase 1 Kernel member-lists is `{Evidence, Provenance}` only
rows.statement: Opens a Kernel candidate matrix (section 10) tabulating candidate/source/why-proposed/counter-evidence/alternative-location/status for: Authority mechanics (RESEARCH_CANDIDATE, contested -- absent from list B), Evidence mechanics (RESEARCH_CANDIDATE, counter-evidence that the kernel must not own typed Assessments), Lifecycle/provenance (RESEARCH_CANDIDATE), KnowledgeProduct (CHALLENGED as too large in its own source document), KnowledgeElement (RESEARCH_CANDIDATE), UNKNOWN-applicability distinction (OPEN, different altitude from v1.1's epistemic UNKNOWN per VC-1), R-CONFLICT as domain invariant (OBSERVED), ChangeSet (RESEARCH_CANDIDATE, implemented so higher evidence class), Rule Port (RESEARCH_CANDIDATE, CONSISTENT with Verification Port), and the Observation/Assessment/Result/Rule-evaluation pipeline (OPEN). No row may reach FORMALLY_ACCEPTED in this ledger -- only the formal architecture can produce that status.

rows.anchor: The kernel protects the rules. The mathematics describes the behavior.
rows.statement: A Phase 1 document (20260822-0021, 995 lines) states the kernel probably will not be a mathematical engine, and prescribes the method order 'existing systems -> discover invariants -> define knowledge concepts -> find mathematical representations -> choose useful formal models', not the reverse ('choose a mathematical model then force knowledge into it'). This is the same verdict the Phase 2 measure-theory thread (proposal 181038 -> five independent K4 refutations -> resolution 192351: 'relational/logical structure as the mathematical core; metric/topology/probability/measure/statistics/causal models as regimes') re-derived on 2026-08-25 under attack, reached roughly four days earlier without book-derived research -- recorded as a convergence to accumulate, not evidence the Phase 2 work was unnecessary, and not a ruling.

rows.anchor: Identity · Evidence · Authority · State · Transition · Provenance · Time · Invariant
rows.statement: A third Phase 1 Kernel member-list (list C, 'formal semantic operating system': Identity, Evidence, Authority, State, Transition, Provenance, Time, Invariant) reintroduces Authority (dropped by list B) and adds four members no earlier list had (Identity, Transition, Time, Invariant); the intersection of all three lists remains {Evidence, Provenance}, unchanged, with the same caution as S1-F003 that an intersection of historical proposals is not a minimality result. List C maps unusually closely onto v1.1's later core-domain primitives (Identity, Authority, History, Verification, Unknown, Contradiction), written ~13 hours before v1.1 -- recorded as UNVERIFIED ATTRIBUTION / co-presence, not descent, since no document asserts the link.
missing: whether v1.1 actually derives from this document -- no document asserts the link

rows.anchor: The single most load-bearing correspondence in the claim is the one that is not a correspondence at all.
rows.statement: Seven of C's eight primitives (Identity, Evidence, Authority, State, Transition, Provenance, Time) name things; the eighth, Invariant, names a constraint on things -- an altitude collapse inside C's own list, unflagged by S1-F005, and it is exactly the item Finding 3 leans on to claim closeness to v1.1 (whose eleven items are all invariants). v1.1 has no PROVENANCE, TIME, STATE, or TRANSITION invariant, and only two of six claimed C-to-v1.1 mappings are clean name matches (Identity, Authority); the rest slash-map (Provenance/History) or match model content/mechanism rather than an invariant.

rows.anchor: Adding a third set to an intersection can only shrink it or leave it unchanged — **never grow it.**
rows.statement: S1-F005 reports 'intersection of all three [A, B, C] remains {Evidence, Provenance} — unchanged by C', arithmetically correct but near-uninformative: since a third set can only shrink or preserve an intersection, and C (eight members from the same vocabulary) contains both existing members, the only way C could have altered the result was by omitting Evidence or Provenance. The informative statement is 'C contains both members of the existing intersection', not that the pair survived a real stability test; those two terms are the most generic available and would survive intersection with nearly any list of epistemic nouns.

rows.anchor: Admission is the act of crossing from candidate to knowledge.
rows.statement: Seven candidate formulations of the core domain act are tested with stated weaknesses (Verification, Admission, Determination, Transformation, Epistemic Maintenance, Justification Preservation, Constitutional Transition); Admission is selected: 'the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state', described as the gate through which all candidates must pass and the culmination of a process. This is the corpus's only place the core act is chosen against explicitly stated alternatives rather than asserted.

rows.anchor: The Kernel owns everything necessary to protect the aggregate invariant during admission, and nothing more.
rows.statement: Hypothesizes the Kernel is 'a domain boundary, not a component' -- a set of rules and invariants governing admission, whose implementation may live in the aggregate but is not the aggregate itself. Proposes an equilibrium criterion balancing two named risks: too small (essential responsibility pushed into mechanisms, aggregate invariant violated, admission boundary bypassed) and too large (God Aggregate absorbing other contexts' responsibilities). Includes: identity assignment, evidence preservation, justification preservation, epistemic state determination, confidence assignment, history recording, constitutional evaluation. Excludes: semantic interpretation, evidence content, reasoning, workflow, Projection, infrastructure -- the first exclusion of Projection found in the corpus, predating the Phase 2 projection thread, given without argument.
missing: specification of which aggregate invariant, singular, the equilibrium protects

rows.anchor: BEST SUPPORTED HYPOTHESIS: 'Kernel as Transformation Boundary (Candidate → Knowledge)'
rows.statement: A fourth boundary formulation is selected after testing four candidates (consistency, decision, admission, transformation boundary): 'Kernel as Transformation Boundary (Candidate -> Knowledge)', protecting 'epistemic coherence invariants' during transformation. Shares S1-F009's 'boundary not component' category but selects a different specific boundary; the source shares S1-F009's numbered-question structure and section headings (same prompt lineage), so their agreement is recorded as weak, non-independent convergence, not corroboration.
missing: a definition of 'epistemic coherence invariants', a new term not otherwise defined in the document

rows.anchor: Hypothesis D: 'Kernel as Epistemic Accountability Core' (derived)
rows.statement: A fifth Kernel formulation: an 'accountable epistemic object' (identity+state+confidence+justification+evidence links+history) protected by a conjunctive invariant (co-consistency and recoverability across all six components), with core act 'epistemic ratification'. Explicitly rejects the 'Kernel as machine' framing (risks reifying it as a workflow component) and, 7 minutes after S1-F011's source, explicitly rejects S1-F011's 'transformation' framing too ('the domain performs status assignment, not content transformation') -- two Phase 2 documents where the later rejects the earlier's selected formulation, unresolved. States an equilibrium bounded by completeness-of-the-act rather than S1-F009's invariant-protection bound, explicitly disclaiming minimalism -- two equilibria that can disagree in practice.

lineage_claims.quote: Transformation of a proposal into knowledge? Strong — but risks implying the domain performs transformation. The domain performs status assignment, not content transformation.

rows.anchor: Model A: "Kernel as Constitutional Distinction-Preservation System"
rows.statement: Three further candidate Kernel models proposed: Model A 'Constitutional Distinction-Preservation System' (owns Identity, Evidence, Justification, EpistemicState, Confidence, History as largely immutable records with History as the sole mutable record; invariants include identity uniqueness and 'history completeness'), Model B 'Epistemic Coherence Boundary', Model C 'Traceable Relationship System'. With these the corpus holds eight distinct Kernel formulations total, six produced within about 13 minutes on 2026-08-23 by model-generated documents sharing one prompt lineage -- recorded as a fact about the corpus, not eight independent arrivals.

rows.anchor: A formulation that was examined and declined is **not** a formulation the corpus holds.
rows.statement: S1-F011's own source tests four boundary candidates (consistency, decision, admission, transformation) before selecting transformation -- so 'consistency boundary' and 'decision boundary' are examined-and-declined options within one document's comparison table, not held positions. On Session 1's own evidence, positions actually taken are admission (F009), transformation (F011), accountability core (F012), plus F013's three models -- six, not eight.

rows.anchor: C is a **fourth question type.**
rows.statement: Two later evidence updates weaken the WHY/WHAT/HOW triad: S1-F005's list C ('kernel primitives': Identity, Evidence, Authority, State, Transition, Provenance, Time, Invariant) answers a composition question with no triad slot, while WHY remains unexemplified across three lists; a second update finds S1-F009 through S1-F013 add at least two further question types (ontological category -- boundary not component, not a machine; and which-specific-boundary selection), leaving WHY empty across eight artifacts and making S2-F010's independently-reached four-question-type reading (membership/boundary/mechanism/semantics) the better-fitting model of the same data -- though not thereby adopted either, and the S2-F011 contradiction (whether list A is protected-concerns or mechanism) remains untouched throughout.

rows.anchor: the law **did** enumerate states, explicitly and with a refusal of an eighth, nearly a day before the document said it did not
rows.statement: v1.1 section 9 (2026-08-22 14:02) enumerates seven epistemic states and explicitly refuses an eighth, about 21.5 hours before S1-F012's source (2026-08-23 11:28) claims the law does not enumerate states -- ruling out a pre-v1.1-snapshot explanation on the dates and establishing the F012 document reasoned from F-1...F-5 material only, second-hand, without v1.1. Consequence: F012's Hypothesis D, selected as 'best supported by existing domain law', is best-supported only by a proper subset of the law, understating how warranted the selection actually is.

lineage_claims.quote: Session 1 flags the Q2 claim as unverified and stops there... it is a probe that reveals the document's reasoning base, and that base is the ground of its central selection.

rows.anchor: A candidate is an interpretation or proposed semantic object. Knowledge is a **ratified domain commitment**.
rows.statement: States a four-way non-collapse pipeline Expression -> Interpretation -> Meaning/Candidate Meaning -> Governance/Admission -> Knowledge, with six stated non-collapses (an expression is not knowledge; an interpretation is not knowledge; a candidate is not knowledge; a mechanism's output is not knowledge; mechanism confidence is not domain confidence; semantic agreement is not truth), and defines Knowledge as 'a ratified domain commitment' -- a sixth genus for Knowledge (after durable understanding, relationship, product-with-members, justified-state-evolution, and capacity), the only genus making an authority ratification act constitutive. Introduces KnowledgeClaim as the post-admission object name, via Candidate -> Admission boundary -> KnowledgeClaim.
invariants: mechanism confidence is not domain confidence

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not synonymous with the Kernel… The Kernel is therefore a proper subset of the KnowledgeOS architecture.
rows.statement: A drafted, PROPOSED (never-adopted) ADR (ADR-KOS-KERNEL-001) is the first corpus document to keep KnowledgeOS, KnowledgeCore, and Kernel apart as three distinct altitudes: KnowledgeOS is not synonymous with the Kernel (Kernel is a proper subset); KnowledgeCore is the bounded context containing the authoritative domain model for admitted knowledge and its constitutional lifecycle; the Kernel is the smallest authoritative protection boundary within KnowledgeCore.

rows.anchor: External contexts may produce expressions, interpretations, candidates, evidence, decisions, projections, or other inputs. Those contexts do not become Kernel responsibilities merely because their outputs are consumed by KnowledgeCore.
rows.statement: States a consumption-boundary policy identified as the sharpest anti-absorption rule in the corpus: external contexts producing expressions/interpretations/candidates/evidence/decisions/projections do not become Kernel responsibilities merely because KnowledgeCore consumes their outputs — blocking the mechanism by which every earlier capability list grew.
invariants: A context does not become a Kernel responsibility merely because its output is consumed by KnowledgeCore

rows.anchor: What is the smallest authoritative boundary that must exist to preserve KnowledgeCore's constitutional invariants? ... The Kernel SHALL therefore be derived from: domain invariants; consistency requirements; …
rows.statement: Defines the Kernel by a question and derivation rule rather than a member-list enumeration: the Kernel is derived from domain invariants and consistency requirements, in direct response to the enumeration-based failure mode diagnosed by S1-F007 and falsified by S1-F016/S1-F017.

rows.anchor: the wider ecosystem · KnowledgeCore as the bounded context · the constitutional/invariant altitude · the smallest executable/authoritative boundary
rows.statement: Names a four-way vocabulary collision on the word 'Kernel' itself within the corpus (the wider ecosystem; KnowledgeCore as bounded context; the constitutional/invariant altitude; the smallest executable/authoritative boundary), proposed as an explanation subsuming several apparent disagreements across earlier findings — documents may have been answering different questions under one word.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS is the preservation and projection infrastructure that records identities, participants, contexts, boundaries, observations, provenance, relations, information histories and transitions ... The KnowledgeOS Kernel is the smallest domain-independent substrate that owns the identity, history, provenance and relational semantics needed to preserve and reconstruct knowledge-bearing activity
rows.statement: Working definition of KnowledgeOS as the preservation and projection infrastructure recording identities, participants, contexts, boundaries, observations, provenance, relations, information histories and transitions needed to reconstruct finite participants' engagements with Knowledge Space, over which external logical/statistical/probabilistic/metric/topological/causal/institutional regimes may operate; and of the Kernel as the smallest domain-independent substrate owning identity, history, provenance and relational semantics needed to preserve and reconstruct knowledge-bearing activity across bounded contexts and mathematical regimes.

rows.anchor: Ātma is not the entire KnowledgeOS kernel implementation. Rather, “Knowledge Ātma” can be the conceptual identity/principle of the kernel.
rows.statement: Knowledge Ātma ≡(conceptual) the persistent identity/principle of the KnowledgeOS Kernel, while 'KnowledgeOS Kernel = the executable realization of that principle' — preserving the concept/implementation distinction. The kernel is what remains structurally stable while Knowledge State K_t, Epistemic State Σ_t and Investigation State Q_t evolve.

rows.anchor: \mathcal{K}_{core}= \{ \text{Identity}, \text{Knowledge State}, \text{Observation}, \text{Evidence}, \text{Epistemic State}, \text{Dimension}, \text{Zero}, \text{Inquiry}, \text{Transition} \}
rows.statement: Proposes a candidate kernel core containing Identity, Knowledge State Model, Observation, Evidence/Provenance, Dimension Discovery, Epistemic State, Coherence, Zero, Investigation, State Transition, and a Knowledge-space interface — explicitly NOT containing all knowledge, only the fundamental mechanisms that make KnowledgeOS a knowledge system; domain knowledge itself stays outside the kernel, giving Kernel ≠ Knowledge (the kernel operates on knowledge, e.g. K_t --Zero--> Δ_t, without needing to know in advance that 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather').

rows.anchor: I would NOT put Lord and Sārathi literally inside the kernel yet
rows.statement: Zero and DimensionDiscovery are treated as kernel capabilities (Zero(K_t,I_t)->Δ_t, DimensionDiscovery(Q,K_t,C)->D), but Lord and Sārathi are explicitly kept OUT of the kernel as a separate 'Epistemic Services' layer above it (Sārathi(K_t,Δ_t,H_t)->a_t still listed but deferred), since there is evidence they are epistemic roles/capabilities but not yet proof they should be kernel primitives — 'later we can determine whether Lord/Sārathi deserve kernel status'.
missing: criteria for promoting a capability to kernel-primitive status

rows.anchor: A_K = \operatorname{Invariant}(S_t)
rows.statement: Gives Ātma a formal manifestation: A_K = Invariant(S_t) where S_{t+1}=δ(S_t,o_t) — the system state evolves (S_0->S_1->S_2->...) while A_K remains invariant, giving architectural form to 'Ātma is the persistent Knower while the state changes'. Composes the full architecture: KnowledgeOS = Knowledge Ātma Kernel + Knowledge Space + Epistemic Capabilities + Domain Knowledge, with the Kernel managing/evolving K_t and K_t⊆𝒦.

rows.anchor: What is the KnowledgeOS Kernel, and which invariants must remain stable while all knowledge states evolve?
rows.statement: Reformulates the planned Question 20 from 'what is the complete system state?' to 'what is the KnowledgeOS Kernel, and which invariants must remain stable while all knowledge states evolve?', framed as necessary to determine what belongs in the Knowledge Ātma Kernel vs KnowledgeOS capabilities vs the domain-specific knowledge space.

rows.anchor:
Conceptual architecture: ~75–80% defined
Mathematical foundations: ~65–70% defined
Executable formal specification: ~40–50% defined
Complete KnowledgeOS theory: ~60–65% defined
rows.statement: Explicit self-assessed maturity percentages, described as architectural judgments not mathematical measurements: conceptual architecture ~75-80%, mathematical foundations ~65-70%, executable formal specification ~40-50%, complete KnowledgeOS theory ~60-65%. Breaks the mathematics into four levels: Ontology (~80-85%, categories {A,D,V,R,E,Σ,G,C,I,Δ,Q,O} mostly identified), Relations (~70%, many pairwise relations Q->D->A->{E,Σ}, but no formally closed complete dependency graph), Dynamics (~55-60%, K_{t+1}=δ(K_t,e_t) and Σ_{t+1}=ε(Σ_t,o_t) exist but event algebra/transition preconditions-invariants/persistence/identity/branching/rollback/concurrency still needed), Calculus/Measurement (~40-50%, the least mature: whether Δ(K,I) is a genuine metric, asymmetry, comparability of missing vs wrong knowledge, uncertainty measurement, incomparable-dimension handling, weight selection, and whether scalarization is even always desirable remain open).

rows.anchor: What exactly is an Observation?
rows.statement: Names four unresolved foundational questions still needed to close the theory: (A) what exactly is an Observation — is Observation=(Observer,Phenomenon,Time,Context,Method,Result) sufficient or is something richer needed; (B) what exactly is a Statement — Statement=(Entity,Dimension,Value) may be too restrictive, needing separate Attribute/Relationship/Existential/Event/Modal/Normative/Causal assertion kinds; (C) whether Relationship (currently R=(E1,E2,D,V)) should instead be a first-class knowledge object carrying its own identity, type, direction, temporal validity, evidence, provenance, context, epistemic state; (D) what makes a candidate dimension legitimate — proposes Candidate(D) -> Evaluate(D,K,P,C) -> Adopt(D)|Reject(D)|Defer(D) as an unresolved evaluation pipeline.

rows.anchor: We have not yet proved a theory. We have constructed a promising formal system whose ontology and invariants are becoming internally coherent.
rows.statement: Recommends the next phase be 'close the theory' rather than 'add more concepts': build one canonical KnowledgeOS mathematical model unifying every object/relationship/invariant/transition established across Questions 1-19, remove duplicated/contradictory definitions, and identify remaining axioms genuinely needed, only THEN proceed to the Knowledge Ātma Kernel implementation architecture. Gives a five-stage position marker: Conceptual Discovery -> Formalization -> [we are here] -> Formal Closure -> Executable Architecture. Triple assessment: as mathematician ('not yet proved a theory'), as DDD architect ('enough bounded concepts to begin defining the Core Domain, but not yet to implement'), as epistemic-system architect (the three Gita chapters were valuable for exposing distinguishing test cases, not for 'proving' KnowledgeOS).

rows.anchor: cost arguments reward **more** Kernel content, invariant arguments reward **less**.
rows.statement: The corpus's cost-based justification for a Kernel (it could change AI computational economics) and its invariant-based justifications (it protects what would otherwise be lost) can produce opposite build/don't-build verdicts from identical evidence: cost arguments reward adding more to the Kernel, invariant arguments reward keeping it minimal. Every 'DO NOT IMPLEMENT (already protected)' verdict in this review register presupposes the invariant framing and could in principle flip under a cost framing.

lineage_claims.quote: Session 1: "the only argument in the entire corpus that justifies a Kernel by what it **saves** rather than by what it **protects**"

rows.anchor: "KnowledgeOS could change the computational economics of AI systems"
rows.statement: The corpus's only economic justification for a Kernel claims KnowledgeOS could change the computational economics of AI systems, but this review finds the economic claim carries no measurements: it is a hypothesis about economics, not evidence, though in principle testable by a benchmark. Verdict: RESEARCH ONLY / PRESERVE, valuable mainly as a warning about verdict-sensitivity rather than as support for building a Kernel.

assumptions.statement: An economically cheaper mechanism justifies inclusion in the Kernel even where law already protects the same invariant.

rows.anchor: re-assessing an acquisition procedure could change knowledge state retroactively
rows.statement: Session 1 derived a consequence, by composing S1-F033's 'knowledge changes when evidence changes' with S1-F030's constitutive acquisition, that re-assessing an acquisition procedure could change knowledge state retroactively, and noted no document addresses this. This review closes the concern: retroactivity is already handled because no member is modified in place without creating a new forward-only state (l. 219); a re-assessment produces a new state while the prior state is retained. Verdict: DO NOT IMPLEMENT.
invariants: no member is modified in place without creating a new forward-only state

rows.anchor: "Does this observation sequence actually **require** explicit duration modelling?"
rows.statement: A conditional proposal -- test whether the observation sequence actually requires explicit duration modelling before assuming it does -- narrows the dissent raised in an earlier semi-Markov tension finding (S1-F032/S2-R-F032), following the same conditional-exclusion form used in S1-F019.

lineage_claims.quote: The conditional proposal narrows `S1-F032`'s dissent.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS may be better understood as a system that **preserves and reconstructs** epistemic states than as a system that stores a primitive called 'Knowledge'. Do not adopt this as truth. **Test it against every new artifact.**
rows.statement: X-004: the reviewer's own standing test hypothesis ('KnowledgeOS may be better understood as preserving/reconstructing epistemic states than storing a Knowledge primitive') appears, worded almost identically, inside the corpus itself (S1-F013 Finding 4, dated 2026-08-23: 'It may be a constitutional system for preserving...') -- before it reached the reviewer as a test instrument. If the hypothesis descends from that corpus material, then five prior per-artifact 'strengthens the hypothesis' confirmations (S2-F024, S2-R-F010/11/12) are framing inheritance, not evidence -- the same circularity failure the reviewer charged Session 1 with elsewhere, now found to apply to itself. Provenance of the hypothesis (from this material, independently, or elsewhere) cannot be established; inferring descent from similarity alone would repeat a prior error (S2-R-F012.1).

lineage_claims.quote: It may be a **constitutional system for preserving**…

rows.anchor: A knowledge system should not merely accumulate representations of reality. It should help an agent distinguish what is known from what is not known, distinguish competing interpretations and permissible actions, determine what remains to be established, choose action within an authorized frame, observe the consequences, and update its state without confusing the new state with the history that produced it.
rows.statement: After Chapters 1-4, one complete philosophical hypothesis is stated and formally adopted as the guiding statement for KnowledgeOS's purpose and as the ongoing philosophical test: a knowledge system should not merely accumulate representations of reality, but should help an agent distinguish what is known from what is not known, distinguish competing interpretations and permissible actions, determine what remains to be established, choose action within an authorized frame, observe the consequences, and update its state without confusing the new state with the history that produced it. The formal ruling accepts the Chapters 1-4 framework as an independent test framework (not a derivation source), adopts no Gita-derived equations as architecture, confirms the three weak points as recommendations for candidate refinement, and establishes a research-track directory structure (research/gita/chapters, principles, tests, synthesis.md) with a fixed eight-stage per-principle recording template (textual observation -> philosophical interpretation -> abstract principle -> KnowledgeOS question -> possible formalization -> mathematical test -> architecture test -> status).

rows.anchor: The KnowledgeOS kernel is conceptually analogous to a mind whose discriminative faculty must continuously evaluate the current epistemic state and possible transformations of that state.
rows.statement: Refinement of the prior hypothesis 'the KnowledgeOS kernel is always busy determining right and wrong' into: the KnowledgeOS kernel is conceptually analogous to a mind whose discriminative faculty must continuously evaluate the current epistemic state and possible transformations of that state, formalized as K_t --Buddhi--> {accept, reject, qualify, revise, defer}.
missing: formal derivation from KnowledgeOS corpus independent of the Gita lens

lineage_claims.quote: This is **much stronger architecturally** than "mind = knowledge."

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition
rows.statement: Central hypothesis: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition, not merely the smallest unit that stores knowledge. Kernel = (State, Transition Capability): the state is what the kernel currently holds, the transition capability determines what can legitimately happen to that state. Gita lens (analytical, not DDD names): Mind -> evolving epistemic state, Buddhi -> discriminative capability, Karma -> action/transition, Phala -> resulting state/outcome.
dependencies: K_t knowledge state at time t

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel: the smallest bounded epistemic mechanism that maintains a time-indexed knowledge state and can discriminate and perform legitimate transitions of that state under the applicable constraints.
rows.statement: Provisional formal kernel definition: K = (K_t, Omega_K, I) where K_t = current knowledge state, Omega_K = permitted kernel operations, I = kernel invariants; K_t --omega in Omega_K--> K_{t+1} only if I(K_t,omega,K_{t+1})=true. Gita gives only the philosophical lens Mind~Kernel, Buddhi~discriminative capability; the mathematical/DDD investigation determines the actual kernel. Key research hypothesis: Kernel != Knowledge Store, but potentially Kernel = Epistemic State + Discrimination + Legitimate State Transition.

rows.anchor: Kernel \neq K_t ... The kernel is the **persistent processing mechanism**, whereas K_t is the **current epistemic state**
rows.statement: Kernel != K_t: since K_t != K_{t+1} (knowledge state changes with time), the Kernel is not any particular knowledge state; the Kernel is the persistent processing mechanism operating on successive knowledge states, analogous to Mind != one particular thought.

rows.anchor: The KnowledgeOS Kernel should not be understood as the whole of knowledge. It is the epistemic mechanism through which a bounded knower processes a changing knowledge state while being unable to directly contain the whole knowledge space.
rows.statement: Strongest Chapter 11 finding: the KnowledgeOS Kernel is not the whole of knowledge but the epistemic mechanism through which a bounded knower processes a changing knowledge state while unable to directly contain the whole knowledge space K. Formalized as Kernel observes/processes a projection of K: O_t = Omega(K_t, K, context), connecting to the previously-established Sanjaya/Omega hypothesis. Chapter 11 corroborates rather than derives this (Step 286 discipline).

lineage_claims.quote: This connects very nicely with the Sanjaya/Omega hypothesis you already established independently.

rows.anchor: Is the KnowledgeOS kernel fundamentally a knowledge-storage mechanism, or is it a discriminative epistemic machine operating on changing knowledge states? ... Kernel \neq K_t
rows.statement: Poses the culminating research question of Chapters 10-14: is the KnowledgeOS kernel fundamentally a storage mechanism, or a discriminative epistemic machine operating on changing knowledge states -- the Gita lens strongly points toward the latter. Formalized: Kernel != K_t; instead Kernel:(K_t,O_t,C_t)->K_{t+1}, with Buddhi subset-of Kernel capability and K_t = state operated upon. Connects this to Step 285's finding that the kernel itself is still not formally selected, keeping this as a new Gita-derived research hypothesis, not canonical. Proposes next step: derive a candidate formal algebra of the Kernel from Chapters 10-14 together, identifying which operations belong to Buddhi vs Mind/Kernel vs transform K_t vs must remain outside the kernel (Governance, authority, provenance).

rows.anchor: \mathcal K \neq K_t \neq \mathcal M
rows.statement: Formal first principle: K (Knowledge Space, potentially unbounded) != K_t (Knowledge State at time t, what the system currently represents) != M (KnowledgeOS Kernel, the smallest persistent computational unit that evaluates and transforms knowledge states). The Gita's language helps interpret M as Mind, but the software kernel is not literally the philosophical mind. Defines M = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition, i.e. capable of K_t->K_{t+1} under some evidence/observation/proposition/event/operation.

rows.anchor: The KnowledgeOS kernel is the smallest epistemic processing unit capable of receiving, discriminating, qualifying, and transforming knowledge-state transitions under constraints.
rows.statement: Culminating candidate answer to 'what is the KnowledgeOS kernel actually for': the KnowledgeOS kernel is the smallest epistemic processing unit capable of receiving, discriminating, qualifying, and transforming knowledge-state transitions under constraints, with Manas=processing, Buddhi=discrimination, Zero=exposure of unresolved epistemic deficiency, delta=state transformation, and Governance=external authority/constraint (kept separate). Proposes a final operator hypothesis set: Omega:W->O (observation), M:O->X (Manas processing), B:XxC->D (Buddhi discrimination), Q:XxD->Q_t (qualification), V:Q_t->{top,bot,?} (verification), Z:X->G (Zero/gap detection), delta:KxO->K' (state transformation) -- explicitly candidate, not canonical; Chapter 16 supplies philosophical evidence and hypotheses only, mathematics/corpus/DDD/Governance still validate each candidate.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest persistent epistemic mechanism capable of representing a knowledge state, discriminating over it, and producing a governed transformation of that state.
rows.statement: Concludes the smallest meaningful kernel cannot be merely a data structure; needs at least Represent + Discriminate + Transform, with Zero/Purification/Action/Guna/provenance understood around this core. Candidate research definition (explicitly not ratified canonical): KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest persistent epistemic mechanism capable of representing a knowledge state, discriminating over it, and producing a governed transformation of that state -- explicitly noting Steps 285-287 deliberately leave canonicalization, equality, Qualify, and governance unresolved.

rows.anchor: GoF and the current KnowledgeOS minimality problem ... Observer is implemented using interface/registration/collection/notification/delegation ... Pattern != Primitive and Pattern != Capability and Pattern != KernelOperation ... A GoF pattern can help implement a capability, but it cannot by itself establish that the capability is necessary.
rows.statement: Connects the implementation-mechanism decomposition (e.g. Observer, Strategy each decomposing into more primitive mechanisms) to the open K_min (kernel minimality) research question, stating Pattern != Primitive, Pattern != Capability, and Pattern != KernelOperation, and that a pattern implementing a capability never by itself establishes that capability's necessity.

lexical.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.

conceptual.anchor: The Kernel is a constitutional decision engine that transforms candidates into admissible knowledge states

formal.anchor: Candidate -> Verification -> Admissibility -> Identity -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge

governance.anchor: no Kernel implementation; no programming-language decision; no database schema; no event-sourcing commitment; no API design; no final aggregate design; no KnowledgeClaim aggregate implementation; no SNF reopening; no real-language corpus experiment; no promotion of an SNF mechanism into KnowledgeOS. The P5 closure remains intact.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.
rationale_evidence.statement: Uses the Linux/Red Hat precedent to argue KnowledgeOS's moat is the kernel plus governance plus evidence model (not the AI model, which is commoditized), proposing a Community/Professional/Enterprise revenue-tier structure and a 10-year IPO roadmap.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Linus did not start by designing 'the operating system of the world.' He started by solving a concrete problem, created a small working kernel ... 'Can we create a trusted kernel that allows digitalization robots to operate safely?'
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not start with an AI-driven Digitalization Robot ambition; the correct starting question is the smallest trusted kernel that later allows robots to operate safely, mirroring Linux's incremental 0.01-kernel-first history.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Open-source the KnowledgeOS Kernel. Commercialize the Digitalization Robot Platform.
rationale_evidence.statement: Recommends an open-core business model (open KnowledgeOS Kernel for trust/ecosystem, commercial Digitalization Robot/Enterprise Platform for revenue), by analogy with Linux Kernel vs Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Rust for the KnowledgeOS Kernel, Kotlin/Spring for the Enterprise Runtime, Python for Intelligence, TypeScript for Experience.
rationale_evidence.statement: Recommends a multi-language technology stack (Rust kernel for memory-safety/correctness, Kotlin+Spring Boot enterprise runtime, Python intelligence layer, TypeScript studio/frontend) with an estimated 12-18 month timeline for a first Kernel v1.0 with a small expert team.

rationale_evidence.anchor: If you want IPO potential, do not position KnowledgeOS as 'AI chatbot' ... nor 'Documentation tool' ... Position as: The operating system for enterprise knowledge and digital transformation.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues the commercial positioning category determines addressable market size; 'AI chatbot' is too easy to copy, 'documentation tool' is too small a category for IPO ambitions.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Kernel scope: 'minimal kernel, no AI' (S0167) vs the platform vision where an AI-driven Digitalization Robot is the top layer (S0171) — the corpus itself frames the robot as a distribution, keeping the kernel AI-free, so the tension is scope of the 'core' vs the 'product'.
rationale_evidence.statement: Surfaces T1: a minimal AI-free kernel proposal versus an AI-driven robot as the platform's top execution layer, resolved by the corpus's own framing (robot = distribution, kernel stays AI-free) but not formally decided.

rationale_evidence.anchor: KNOWLEDGEOS KERNEL protects: identity · evidence · provenance · lifecycle · authority · invariants · temporal state / higher layers provide: assurance · analytics · inference · simulation · AI · visualization · delivery ... a PROPOSED KERNEL BOUNDARY CANDIDATE, outline supported, provenance+temporal weak.
rationale_evidence.statement: H-10: tests the seven-concern kernel/higher-layer split against all three baselines per-concern; identity, evidence, lifecycle, authority, and invariants are supported, provenance and temporal state are weak, so the overall split is a candidate outline, not an established fact.

rationale_evidence.anchor: WHAT IS THE CORE DOMAIN ACT? ... Verification | Admission | Determination | Transformation | Epistemic Maintenance | Justification Preservation | Constitutional Transition
rationale_evidence.statement: Seven alternative formulations of KnowledgeOS's core domain act are compared (Verification, Admission, Determination, Transformation, Epistemic Maintenance, Justification Preservation, Constitutional Transition), each with its domain-meaning implication.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Candidate -> Verification -> Admissibility -> Identity -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge
rationale_evidence.statement: Admission is modelled as a distinction chain (Candidate -> Verification[well-formed?] -> Admissibility[constitution?] -> Identity[stable anchor?] -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge) and as an 8-step process from candidate proposal to emission of KnowledgeCreated.

rationale_evidence.anchor: KnowledgeCreated is the domain event that signals the completion of admission.
rationale_evidence.statement: KnowledgeCreated is analyzed as the domain event signalling completion of admission -- the business moment the candidate becomes part of KnowledgeOS with identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all established; the Kernel's job is to produce this event on success and nothing/a rejection on failure.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The Kernel owns everything necessary to protect the aggregate invariant during admission, and nothing more.
rationale_evidence.statement: Tests a 'small kernel' hypothesis against two risks -- too small (essential responsibility leaks into mechanisms, e.g. ML evidence weighting; aggregate invariant violated; admission boundary bypassed) and too large (God Aggregate absorbing interpretation/workflow) -- and proposes the equilibrium principle that the Kernel owns exactly what is necessary to protect the aggregate invariant during admission and nothing more.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Hypothesis A: Kernel as Admission Boundary / Hypothesis B: Kernel as Epistemic Decision Core / Hypothesis C: Kernel as Knowledge Consistency Boundary / Hypothesis D: Kernel as Constitutional Transition Engine
rationale_evidence.statement: Four competing Kernel hypotheses (A: Admission Boundary owning identity/evidence/justification/epistemic-state/confidence/history; B: Epistemic Decision Core owning only epistemic-state/confidence/evidence-sufficiency/justification, excluding identity/history; C: Knowledge Consistency Boundary owning invariants/contradictions/history/provenance; D: Constitutional Transition Engine owning rule application) are each given domain purpose, owned concepts, invariants, strengths, weaknesses, and DDD risks; Hypothesis A is judged best supported by the existing F-1..F-5 domain law, with B/C/D framed as partial views.

rationale_evidence.anchor: CandidateProposed -> CandidateAdmitted -> KnowledgeCreated -> KnowledgeQualified -> KnowledgeContested -> KnowledgeSuperseded ... It may instead be the domain authority for transitions of epistemic state.
rationale_evidence.statement: Domain-event lens critique: questions whether KnowledgeCreated is truly the fundamental domain event or merely the first event of a longer lifecycle (CandidateProposed -> CandidateAdmitted -> KnowledgeCreated -> KnowledgeQualified -> KnowledgeContested -> KnowledgeSuperseded); if so the Kernel may not be a creation/admission engine but the domain authority for transitions of epistemic state generally.

rationale_evidence.anchor: DeepSeek lists confidence alongside identity, evidence and history as universally mandatory. That is not yet established. ... Model A - confidence is intrinsic / Model B - confidence is an epistemic assessment / Model C - confidence is a contextual projection
rationale_evidence.statement: Epistemic lens critique disputes that confidence is necessarily a Kernel invariant, proposing three competing models: (A) confidence intrinsic to Knowledge; (B) confidence as a derived epistemic assessment over evidence; (C) confidence as a contextual projection of evidence; warns that under B or C, making confidence a fundamental Kernel invariant could wrongly couple the Kernel to an assessment mechanism.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Core act 🟢 Strong hypothesis | Admission boundary 🟢 Strong | Aggregate reasoning 🟡 Needs proof | Constitutional boundary 🟡 Needs separation | Confidence ownership 🔴 Unproven | History ownership 🟡 Unproven | Evidence ownership 🟡 Needs refinement | Lifecycle scope 🔴 Underexplored | EKS/PKS historical continuity 🔴 Missing | SNF implications 🟡 Needs explicit integration | Sanskrit/compiler lens 🟡 Missing | Bounded-context boundary 🟡 Needs deeper analysis | Kernel capacity 🟡 Prematurely broad
rationale_evidence.statement: A 13-row scorecard grades DeepSeek's brainstorming area-by-area (green/yellow/red), rating the core-act hypothesis and admission-boundary framing strong, but aggregate reasoning, constitutional boundary, confidence ownership, history ownership, evidence ownership, lifecycle scope, EKS/PKS historical continuity, SNF integration, and the Sanskrit/compiler lens all as unproven, missing, or needing more work.

sources.note: The migration plan for B' relocation and its full amendment/independent-review chain (S0131, S0133-S0142, S0146), including the recurring self-review-exposure pattern and the single safety-critical finding DV-1.

rows.anchor: Governance does not treat a later-arriving text as automatically governing... a later act is not automatically a supersession.
rows.statement: A later-arriving instruction/act is not automatically treated as superseding a prior, already-executed one; which text governs is a disposition the PO/ARB must make explicitly.

rows.anchor: What a self-review CAN establish...What it CANNOT establish...that the migration design is sound...that its findings are right...that nothing was omitted that the author did not think of
rows.statement: A self-review (same producer as the artifact under review) explicitly states it can establish mechanical completeness and provenance (re-runnable by anyone) but cannot establish design soundness, correctness of findings, or omissions the author itself did not think of; states it must never be cited as independent verification.

rows.anchor: INFO-1 — a defect this pass found in its own artifact... The plan should scope the claim as 'exactly one writer OF GOVERNANCE EVIDENCE' and cite the discriminating test.
rows.statement: The plan's claim of 'exactly one writer' is correct but not reproducible from the obvious grep, which returns three files; the discriminating test (references runtime/workflow AND writes) is what makes the claim survive, and the plan should scope its own claim accordingly.

rows.anchor: the S4b lane's registered executionContext names the producer as claude-code-session:5e1dd9ee. The plan 3817eb2b was produced by claude-code-session:1c8b041b.
rows.statement: INFO-2: a provenance discrepancy exists in the governance record itself (not the plan) — the plan discloses its own producer correctly, but the lane's registered executionContext names a different process as producer; reconciling this is left as a Governance act.

rows.anchor: the §1 inventory is a point-in-time measurement of a LIVE corpus... §1's numbers are a dated observation, not the migration's inventory, and must not be substituted for the Phase-1 run.
rows.statement: INFO-4: the plan's own current-state inventory numbers are only a dated snapshot of a corpus that continues to accept writes, and must never be substituted for the migration's own required Phase-1 inventory run.

rows.anchor: Verified: the CONDITION was recorded two days earlier, in 2026-08-17-KOS-ATTR-ARCH-001-stage2-bounded-context-confirmation.md as coupling problem C-2
rows.statement: Corrects the premise that a migration-plan finding is 'new evidence': the underlying condition (interpretation authority is environment-swappable via KOS_MECHANISM_PATH) was already recorded two days earlier as coupling problem C-2 with its own remedy route (R-37/ADR-C6); what the migration plan added was precision (a two-axis formulation and line-addressed evidence), not discovery.

lineage_claims.quote: What the migration plan added is PRECISION, not discovery

rows.anchor: The Single Authority Resolver invariant is explicitly extended from governance-evidence record location to also govern the mechanism that interprets those records...an EXPLICIT SCOPE EXTENSION, not as an application of the existing invariant.
rows.statement: Decision: Option A (bring the interpreter-selection axis under the same resolver boundary as the record-location axis) is adopted, but recorded explicitly as a deliberate scope extension of the existing invariant rather than a silent application of it, so that the estate's rule against silent scope expansion is honoured.

rows.anchor: the delivered plan already presumes A... The two delivered artifacts are not aligned: the plan implements an answer the review says is not yet given.
rows.statement: Observes that the migration plan's Phase 5 already operationally assumes Option A (bringing the interpreter mechanism under the resolver) while the governance review states the question is not yet determined and that governance must not determine it — an internal misalignment between two delivered artifacts that the pending decision must resolve.

rows.anchor: This review establishes: completeness · provenance · conformity to decided governance constraints. It CANNOT and does NOT establish: technical soundness · implementation correctness · migration safety · production readiness.
rows.statement: An independent (different producer) governance review explicitly separates what it establishes (completeness, provenance, conformity to decided constraints, all re-executed rather than re-read) from what only a separate technical Architecture review may establish (soundness, correctness, safety, readiness).

rows.anchor: INFO-1 — the inventory figures have drifted by one, and the drift is fully accounted for.
rows.statement: Re-measures the corpus independently and finds a one-grant drift from the plan's cited figures, traces it exactly to a governance act registered after the plan's commit, and confirms the plan was accurate at its own commit — demonstrating the corpus's live-growth property with concrete numbers.

rows.anchor: 23 / 30 ... trials that lost a transition ... exit status of the losing process 0 — accepted, reported {"ok":true,"seq":2} ... sequence set of every survivor DENSE and MONOTONIC
rows.statement: A concurrency experiment run in a temp directory (never against the real corpus) launched two concurrent `append` calls against the workflow-state.php writer 30 times; 23 of 30 trials silently lost a transition, the losing process reported success (exit 0), and the surviving sequence remained dense and monotonic every time — the same loss reproduced on the `grant` write path.

assumptions.statement: no lock, lease, or CAS exists around the read-modify-write cycle
assumptions.anchor: the header says so plainly: 'Increment 2 is not authorized: no lock, no lease, no hook, no enforcement.'

experiment.hypothesis: Concurrent appends to the governance-evidence writer can silently drop a transition while leaving the sequence dense and monotonic.
experiment.setup: Two `php workflow-state.php append` invocations run concurrently (backgrounded, `wait`) against a fresh temp work item, 30 trials; same test repeated on the `grant` path.
experiment.assumptions: No lock/lease/CAS/hook exists on the read-modify-write cycle around loadRecord/assertTransitionAllowed/saveRecord.
experiment.inputs: A freshly initialized work item directory (mktemp -d), two REGISTER-type append payloads per trial.
experiment.method: Run both appends in parallel via shell backgrounding, then inspect the resulting record for transition count, sequence values, and exit codes of both processes.
experiment.result: 23/30 trials lost a transition; every losing process exited 0; survivor sequence sets were dense and monotonic ([1,2]) in every trial, including the lossy ones; the grant path lost G-ONE in one run with exit 0.
experiment.interpretation: Density and monotonicity of the sequence are preserved BY the loss (the clobbering writer reuses the lost writer's seq number), so they are not evidence of completeness.
experiment.limitations: Run only in a temp directory via --dir override, never against .claude/runtime/ itself; rate (77%) bounds likelihood under this specific contention pattern, not a general guarantee.
experiment.conclusion: The plan's premise that dense/monotonic seq is what makes reconciliation mechanically decidable is true for deciding STRICT EXTENSION vs PREFIX DISAGREEMENT, but does not extend to a completeness guarantee, and the plan had used it for both.

rows.anchor: session-resolve.php EXECUTES an arbitrary program named by the environment and HANDS IT the authority record directory as an argument. ⇒ This is not only an interpretation path. It is a WRITE path
rows.statement: session-resolve.php is found to be stronger a hazard than the plan states: it executes a subprocess named by the KOS_MECHANISM_PATH environment variable and passes it the authority record directory as an argument, making it a write path through a component whose own bytes contain no write call — a hazard whose value rises once relocation makes the target the durable authoritative store.

rows.anchor: the durable artifact is a git blob, and git — not the copy — decides the committed bytes... a clone on a CRLF platform materialises different bytes and the Phase-4 hashes no longer verify
rows.statement: Byte-preservation of the migration copy is undermined by an unpinned .gitattributes (`* text=auto`, eol unspecified): checkout normalisation is a no-op today (no CR bytes exist), but a future clone on a CRLF platform would materialise different bytes and invalidate the Phase-4 hashes, and the plan's own scope fence names .gitignore but is silent about .gitattributes, the file that actually governs committed bytes.

rows.anchor: PASS WITH DESIGN CLARIFICATIONS ... CL-1–CL-3 are GATES ON PHASE 3 — the migration must not begin until they are closed.
rows.statement: Verdict: PASS WITH DESIGN CLARIFICATIONS, twelve items (CL-1..CL-12) ranked, of which CL-1 (concurrency/completeness claim must be bounded, not absolute), CL-2 (Phase 1 inventory must be re-executed and frozen at migration time, not pinned to a stale literal), and CL-3 (the plan names no act that produces the resolver it later switches to) are gate-class and block Phase 3 from beginning; none requires reopening B', R-CONFLICT, OPEN-M3, or placement governance.

rows.anchor: the withdrawal is real ... NO SILENT REINTRODUCTION FOUND. The stronger claim does not survive anywhere in the artifact.
rows.statement: CL-1 (concurrency/completeness) is verified CLOSED: AMD3's bounded restatement ('no record lost RELATIVE TO the frozen manifest and both inputs') is checked at every site in the artifact and the withdrawn absolute claim is not silently reintroduced anywhere.

rows.anchor: RC-4 — NEW GAP the remedy does not cover ... A write landing after the Phase-5 re-hash but before the writer is switched goes to the RUNTIME copy ... and is destroyed by Phase 7.
rows.statement: RC-4: the freeze/manifest/re-hash design verifies the runtime copy at exactly one instant (the Phase-5 re-hash), three phases before the destructive Phase-7 removal; a write landing in that gap is in neither the frozen manifest nor either reconciliation input and would be silently destroyed by Phase 7's removal, which relies on a byte-verification performed earlier and never rechecked.

rows.anchor: RC-1 ... Phase 2b as written is CIRCULAR with Phase 3, and Phase 3's precondition is therefore unsatisfiable.
rows.statement: RC-1: as amended, a phase that pins .gitattributes AND commits the Phase-1 manifest in the same commit as the Phase-3 copy cannot complete before Phase 3 (its commit must contain Phase 3's output), while Phase 3 cannot begin before that phase completes — the same defect class as CL-3 (a phase consuming an artifact its own predecessor has not produced) reappearing inside a remedy meant to close a different clarification.

rows.anchor: RC-2 — but the OTHER half of INV-R1's row-1 cell was not split, and it collides with both contract suites... an implementer who applies the boundary check literally makes the entire pinned contract suite exit 65 with no report.
rows.statement: RC-2: every test in both pinned contract suites drives the components through a --dir temp path outside the governed evidence boundary, so a literal reading of the resolver's boundary-validation rule would make the entire pinned suite refuse with no report; the fix requires stating that a governed override selects a non-authoritative output location rather than violating the boundary.

rows.anchor: RC-10 — a mis-resolved path MATERIALIZES rather than failing ... The writer creates its parent directory.
rows.statement: RC-10: saveRecord() calls mkdir on its target's parent directory, meaning a resolver that returns a wrong-but-well-formed path does not fail loudly but silently manufactures a new evidence location — recreating the exact misfiling defect B' exists to close, inside the component built to close it; the refusal must therefore be enforced before saveRecord is reached.

rows.anchor: RC-9 — 'canonical re-encode' is not defined ... a false CASE B (escalation) rather than a false CASE A (silent merge) — the safe direction
rows.statement: RC-9: the plan's 'common prefix byte-identical' comparison rule for CASE A does not define its canonicalization method (e.g. key-order sorting), and since JSON decode/encode preserves insertion order, two semantically equal but differently-ordered records would compare unequal, producing a false escalation to CASE B rather than a false silent merge (CASE A) — the safe failure direction, but ambiguous as written.

rows.anchor: DI-1 ... DUPLICATE CURRENT SECTION IDENTIFIERS, introduced by AMD4 itself. ## 4.1 occurs at line 349 ... AND at line 436
rows.statement: DI-1: AMD4 itself introduced duplicate section headings ('## 4.1' occurring twice, '## 4.2' occurring twice) with live cross-references binding ambiguously to both senses, including inside the very finding (RC-4) meant to protect the irreversible removal step; section order also became non-monotonic.

rows.anchor: DI-3 — §11.1's heading asserts 'there are SIX' over an eight-row table, and no grouping of the rows yields six.
rows.statement: DI-3: a dependency table's own summary heading claims six prerequisites while the table mechanically contains eight rows and no grouping of the rows sums to six — an enumeration-versus-content mismatch of the same shape as RC-7a (an argument enumerating fewer items than its own change set).

rows.anchor: RD-7 — no phase RETRACTS the staging marker ... after the writer switch the AUTHORITATIVE store carries an on-disk NON-AUTHORITATIVE label — the exact reader-visible contradiction the marker exists to prevent.
rows.statement: RD-7: AMD4's staging-store marker is given a stated lifetime ('from Phase 2 until Phase 5') but no phase actually removes it; since the staging store is committed durably, the consequence is that after the writer switch, the now-authoritative store carries a durable, versioned, on-disk NON-AUTHORITATIVE label — exactly the contradiction the marker exists to prevent.

rows.anchor: RD-3 — Phase-7 mismatch disposition routes post-demotion writes into §6 CASE A, which would import non-authoritative bytes that §8 says require a governance act
rows.statement: RD-3: AMD4 routes every Phase-7 mismatch to the same reconciliation logic (CASE A/B), but CASE A appends the runtime tail as a legitimate extension, meaning a post-writer-switch write to the demoted store would be silently imported into the authoritative store — contradicting the plan's own rule that re-promoting a demoted source is a governance act, not a merge.

rows.anchor: C-4 ... Phase 5's own bookkeeping is a gap-window write BY CONSTRUCTION, and freezing the order without deciding where it lands ships the defect again.
rows.statement: Addendum: the reviewer flags five defects (C-1..C-5) in a drafted-but-not-yet-executed AMD6 commission, the most consequential being that Phase 5's own re-hash/reconciliation evidence is itself a gap-window write, so freezing the sequence without deciding where that evidence is recorded would reproduce RD-10's exact degradation at the irreversible gate; recommends recording the switch-over evidence into the new store, after the switch.

rows.anchor: The exposure changed shape rather than disappearing... RC-1…RC-11 are ADDRESSED, never CLOSED. The bound recurs until an amendment produces no new remedy.
rows.statement: Names a structural pattern in the amendment chain: an independent review's findings are 'CLOSED' only by a later independent review, but the amendment that repairs them is itself always authored by the same non-independent producer and so is only ever 'ADDRESSED,' never self-closed — this exposure recurs at every amendment until one adds no new remedy.

rows.anchor: CASE α — pre-writer-switch ... RECONCILE under §6 ... CASE β — post-writer-switch ... not authoritative — written against a demoted store ... QUARANTINE · record the conflict · ESCALATE. Never imported.
rows.statement: AMD5 splits the Phase-7 mismatch disposition into two named cases with opposite treatment: CASE α (pre-writer-switch, authoritatively-produced bytes) reconciles under the existing R-CONFLICT logic, while CASE β (post-writer-switch, written against an already-demoted store) is quarantined, recorded as a conflict, and escalated — never imported — with a conservative tie-break (unresolvable ordering defaults to CASE β).
missing: a terminating condition for CASE β — later found missing by the AMD5 review

rows.anchor: the freeze PARTITIONS writes instead of prohibiting all of them ... The freeze keeps its evidential value because the test changed from 'did anything change?' to 'did anything change that we did not declare?'
rows.statement: Repairs RD-10 by partitioning the migration's declared write freeze into prohibited (unrelated corpus appends, a violation) versus permitted-and-declared-in-advance (the migration lane's own governance records), so the freeze's detection test changes from an unreachable 'nothing changed' to a checkable 'nothing changed that we did not declare'.

rows.anchor: The AMD4 additions moved and the originals did not, deliberately: renumbering the originals would have invalidated citations in two already-delivered independent reviews.
rows.statement: A citation-preservation convention: when repairing duplicate section numbering, only the newly-added (colliding) sections are renumbered; the original section numbers are kept even though non-monotonic locally, specifically to avoid invalidating citations already made in delivered independent reviews.

rows.anchor: RD-7·b — the closure claim is stronger than the design it describes ... throughout steps 3→4→5 the store that is already authoritative is on-disk labelled NON-AUTHORITATIVE
rows.statement: AMD5's remedy claims the authoritative store is 'at NO point' labelled NON-AUTHORITATIVE, but this is false for the interval between the writer switch (step 3) and the marker retraction (step 5); the residual is the same class the AMD4 review already accepted for a different window (RD-2) and is not itself unsafe, but the claim overstates what was achieved and must be restated rather than denied.

rows.anchor: RD-3·a — CASE β has no terminating condition, and criteria 12 and 15 are jointly unsatisfiable in it ... after a β event the runtime source therefore never equals manifest + reconciled delta, so §4.4's own gate can never be satisfied
rows.statement: Two of AMD5's own acceptance criteria are jointly unsatisfiable after a CASE β event: criterion 12 requires the runtime source to equal 'manifest + reconciled delta' before removal, but criterion 15 defines CASE β bytes as deliberately never reconciled, so the removal gate could never be satisfied, be permanently blocked, or be satisfied only by destroying the quarantined bytes — none of which the plan states.
missing: a stated terminating condition — the residual this finding identifies

rows.anchor: the strongest statement made must never exceed the strength of the available evidence.
rows.statement: States a general reviewing standard, applied throughout the chain: 'the plan's own standard applies: the strongest statement made must never exceed the evidence' — used specifically to argue that RD-7's genuinely-fixed defect should be restated as bounded rather than denied as fully closed.

rows.anchor: CASE B (§6: same sequence, different content) and CASE β (§4.4: post-demotion write) are different classes with near-identical glyphs ⇒ rename one pair.
rows.statement: DI-7: identifies a glyph collision between two unrelated concepts sharing near-identical names (Latin 'CASE B' meaning same-sequence-different-content, vs Greek 'CASE β' meaning post-demotion write), live inside an operator-facing rollback section, and recommends renaming only the newer family to avoid invalidating citations in already-delivered reviews.

rows.anchor: DV-1 — the durable copy is written twice after its last all-or-nothing verification and is re-verified nowhere before Phase 7 removes the source ... the surviving authoritative store would be the unverified one
rows.statement: DV-1, the single UNSAFE-direction finding across the whole amendment chain: after Phase 4's verification, the durable copy is written twice more (a reconciliation write and a carry-across write) before the writer switch, and the Phase-7 removal gate compares the source against a recorded enumeration whose operands are independent of the copy's actual content — so a silent copy-side write failure would pass every specified gate and the source (the only verified copy) would then be destroyed, leaving the unverified copy as sole authority, defeating B' for those records.

rows.anchor: an undisposed conflict means the migration aggregate CANNOT LEGITIMATELY TRANSITION TO ITS COMPLETED STATE — so the block is not a tooling limitation to be engineered away, it is the aggregate refusing an invalid transition.
rows.statement: Reframes the Phase-7 quarantine block (RD-3·a's fix) as a DDD domain-state-transition concept rather than an implementation limitation: an undisposed quarantine means the migration's own domain aggregate cannot legitimately transition to COMPLETED — the same discipline is applied to naming the disposal actor (a proposed reading by extension, explicitly not a decision) and to measuring, rather than assuming, that no DISPOSE transition exists in the workflow engine's vocabulary.

rows.anchor: DV-3 ... 'the FIRST record in the authoritative store' is false under the plan's own record vocabulary, at four sites including criterion 17
rows.statement: DV-3: the acceptance criterion's claim that the switch-over record is 'the first record in the authoritative store' is false under either of the plan's own definitions of 'record' (a work-item file, or a transition entry); the true and sufficient claim is that it is 'the first GOVERNANCE APPEND made into the authoritative store after the writer switch,' a distinction the plan already has vocabulary for but does not use in the acceptance criterion.

rows.anchor: DV-6 ... A post-demotion record is OUTSIDE the enumeration by definition. Moving it out of the demoted store therefore makes the source MATCH the enumeration ⇒ the final re-hash reports identical ⇒ criterion 12's removal branch opens while a quarantine stands undisposed.
rows.statement: DV-6: the plan's stated reason for forbidding a MOVE of a quarantined record is inverted — moving the record OUT of the demoted store would actually make the source spuriously MATCH the recorded enumeration and open the removal gate while an undisposed quarantine still stands, a subtler variant of the 'remove the store to pass the check' laundering path; the rule itself is correctly (doubly) guarded elsewhere, only its stated justification is wrong.

rows.anchor: C-9 ... The track label was not used as a key ... no aggregate created, initialised or forked
rows.statement: Aggregate-identity verification is performed directly from the governance record's own workItem/workflow fields (not the human-readable track label used in prose) to confirm all four AMD6 commission grants live inside the single canonical aggregate record, with the corpus record count unchanged before and after.

rows.anchor: a finding is M (mechanical) if a deterministic checker over the artifact could have produced it with no architectural judgement... 29 % → 46 % → 58 %
rows.statement: Classifying every new finding across the AMD3/AMD4/AMD5 independent reviews as mechanical (M) or judgement (J) shows the mechanical share rose from 29% (4/14) to 46% (6/13) to 58% (7/12) as the migration-plan design stabilised — a measured trend across three independent reviewers, none of whom was looking for it, showing an increasing share of scarce independent-architecture review capacity was spent on machine-catchable defects.

rows.anchor: TRAP 1 — the comparison object ... If Architecture specifies 're-run Phase 4', the comparison object is the FROZEN MANIFEST, which predates the reconciled delta and the pre-switch Phase-5 records ⇒ THE CHECK FAILS IN THE NORMAL CASE, and DV-1's repair reproduces DV-2's defect inside itself.
rows.statement: Flags that a naive repair of DV-1 (re-verifying the durable copy against the original frozen manifest) would fail in the normal case, because the manifest predates the reconciled delta and pre-switch records; the comparison object must instead be the already-closed SOURCE FINAL-STATE ENUMERATION, or DV-1's own fix would silently reproduce DV-2's self-satisfying-gate defect.

rows.anchor: HO-1 ... the plan already closes the enumeration BEFORE the final copy-side write, and the write DEPENDS on it ... the copy cannot be brought to a state that has not yet been closed, so the handoff's order cannot be executed as written.
rows.statement: An unregistered authoring-handoff draft inverted a data dependency: it proposed closing the SOURCE FINAL-STATE ENUMERATION after the final copy-side write, but the copy-side write's own target IS that enumeration, so the enumeration must close first; the fix requires exactly one new sub-step (verify the copy against the already-closed enumeration) rather than a second construction site for the object.

rows.anchor: ATTACK 9 — Is OR-MERGE mandated, or merely convenient? *** THE DECISIVE ONE *** ... If Sigma is STORED and merged with OR: state stays (1,1) (Conflict) FOREVER — OR is monotone, so no merge can ever clear the R bit. If Sigma is DERIVED from the evidence set: state correctly becomes Supported. **LANDS — and it decides D-4.** OR-merge is correct ONLY IF Sigma is DERIVED from the evidence set. A STORED Sigma under OR-merge cannot recover from Retract, contradicting 272B's own operation set.
rows.statement: ATTACK 9 (marked 'THE DECISIVE ONE') lands and directly resolves decision D-4 (is Sigma stored or derived?): OR-based merge (sigma1 ⊔ sigma2 = (s1∨s2, r1∨r2)) is monotone, so if Sigma is stored as accumulated state, a Refute-then-Retract sequence (evidence e1=Support, e2=Refute reaching Conflict, then Retract(e2)) leaves the stored value permanently at Conflict since OR can never clear a bit -- yet Step 272B's own operation set includes Retract, and correctly recomputing Sigma from the current evidence set after Retract gives Supported, not Conflict. Conclusion: Sigma must be DERIVED (recomputed from the live evidence set) rather than stored/accumulated, or the theory contradicts its own Retract operation.

lineage_claims.target: a stored/accumulated Sigma under OR-merge, vs Step 272B's own Retract operation

experiment.hypothesis: Sigma can be validly implemented as a stored value updated via OR-merge as new evidence arrives.
experiment.setup: Simulate an evidence sequence: e1 supports (S bit set), e2 refutes (R bit set, giving Conflict), then e2 is retracted.
experiment.assumptions: Retract is a valid, required operation in O_sem (per Step 272A); OR-merge is the proposed update rule for a stored Sigma.
experiment.inputs: Evidence list [(e1,Support),(e2,Refute)], then retraction of e2.
experiment.method: Compare the Sigma value obtained by (a) OR-merging into a stored accumulator across the evidence sequence including the retraction, versus (b) recomputing Sigma fresh from the current (post-retraction) evidence set.
experiment.result: (a) stored+OR-merge stays at Conflict=(1,1) forever, since OR-merge cannot clear the R bit; (b) fresh recomputation correctly yields Supported=(1,0).
experiment.interpretation: A stored Sigma updated via OR-merge is incompatible with Retract ever being effective on the epistemic status.
experiment.limitations: Assumes OR-merge is the only proposed update rule; a different (non-monotone) merge/update rule was not tested.
experiment.conclusion: D-4 (is Sigma stored or derived?) is answered: Sigma must be derived from the live evidence set, not stored as an accumulated value under OR-merge.
