sources.note: External-literature research base (Truth Maintenance Systems, AGM belief revision, justification logic, 2025 epistemic-integrity framework, provenance-enhanced knowledge graphs) proposing a candidate Epistemic-Operating-System architecture and five candidate invariants EPI-001..005; explicitly not an established academic pattern.

rows.anchor: External research provides strong theoretical foundations for epistemic reasoning systems, but does not establish "Epistemic Operating System" as a canonical architecture pattern.
rows.statement: Executive summary of an external-literature research pass: the term 'Epistemic Operating System' does not exist as an established academic concept; three core subsystems are identified as required for epistemically robust reasoning -- belief management, contradiction detection, truth constraint enforcement.

rows.anchor: A truth maintenance system (TMS) is the collection of procedures and data structures used for accomplishing belief revision. ... no belief is kept without a reason.
rows.statement: Truth Maintenance System (TMS) definition and core task cited from external research (Martins & Shapiro 1991): maintain conclusions such that (1) not known contradictory, (2) no belief kept without a reason. Two approaches: single-context (JTMS/LTMS) vs multiple-context (ATMS/MBR).

rows.anchor: Expansion (K + phi) / Contraction (K - phi) / Revision (K * phi) ... AGM Postulates for Revision (K*1-K*8)
rows.statement: AGM (Alchourron, Gardenfors, Makinson) belief revision theory cited: three basic operations (Expansion, Contraction, Revision) and the eight AGM postulates K*1..K*8 for revision, plus the semantic interpretation 'AGM revision equivalent to total preorders'.

rows.anchor: Epistemic logic with justification, along with the usual knowledge operator, contains assertions t:F (t is a justification for F). ... Knowledge is true justified belief (Plato)
rows.statement: Justification logic (Artemov 2004) cited: extends epistemic logic with explicit justification terms t:F; distinguishes Ki-phi (agent i knows phi, justified true belief) from Bi-phi (agent i believes phi, may be false/unjustified); extends to multi-agent distributed/common knowledge.

rows.anchor: Structured belief base B_t with accompanying justification graph ... Immutable evidence E* as external reference for validation ... Cryptographically verifiable ledger for epistemic history ... Minimal-mutilation principles for revision
rows.statement: Recent (June 2025) 'Structuring Epistemic Integrity in Artificial Reasoning Systems' framework cited: requires evidentialist constraints, Bayesian updating, logical closure schemas; components include structured belief base B_t, immutable evidence E*, dependency-directed backtracking, cryptographically verifiable ledger, minimal-mutilation revision principles.

rows.anchor: Belief Management | Contradiction Detection | Truth Constraint Enforcement | Justification Tracking | Provenance Management | Revision Protocol
rows.statement: Candidate Epistemic Operating System architecture: six core subsystems (Belief Management, Contradiction Detection, Truth Constraint Enforcement, Justification Tracking, Provenance Management, Revision Protocol) plus data structures (structured belief base B_t, justification graph DAG, immutable evidence E*, epistemic ledger, cognitive worlds) and five invariants (epistemic consistency, justificatory transparency, minimal mutilation, global acyclicity, truth preservation).

rows.anchor: No established "Epistemic OS" pattern: The term is emerging, not canonical ... Limited integration with organizational governance ... Human-AI epistemic collaboration ... Temporal epistemic logic
rows.statement: Six identified research gaps: no established Epistemic-OS pattern; limited integration with organizational governance; TMS/RMS scalability challenges; limited probabilistic/symbolic integration; limited human-AI epistemic collaboration research; limited bi-temporal epistemic logic research.

rows.anchor: EPI-001: Justification Transparency. Draft: Every belief must have an explicit, auditable justification graph. Evaluation: Strongly supported. Classification: Strong candidate.
rows.statement: Five candidate invariants for an Epistemic Operating System, each tested against cited research and classified: EPI-001 Justification Transparency (strong candidate), EPI-002 Epistemic Consistency (strong candidate), EPI-003 Minimal Mutilation (candidate), EPI-004 Provenance Homogeneity (research hypothesis), EPI-005 Immutable Evidence Reference (research hypothesis).

rows.anchor: No belief is kept without a reason. ... KnowledgeOS must preserve: Decision -> justification -> AI summary -> source document. The chain matters.
rows.statement: TMS's 'no belief without a reason' is claimed to strengthen the Transformation Integrity candidate invariant: a Document->AI Summary->Decision chain must preserve the full justification chain back to the source document.

rows.anchor: 1. Justification Integrity: Every derived knowledge state SHALL preserve an explicit justification chain. ... 2. Belief/Core Separation ... 3. Revision Integrity ... 4. Provenance Context: Knowledge meaning SHALL include the provenance conditions under which it is valid.
rows.statement: Four un-numbered candidate invariants proposed for promotion from the epistemic-OS research review: (1) Justification Integrity (every derived knowledge state SHALL preserve an explicit justification chain, per TMS/RMS/justification logic), (2) Belief/Core Separation (derived conclusions SHALL remain distinguishable from authoritative knowledge, per TMS/RMS), (3) Revision Integrity (knowledge evolution SHALL preserve minimal justified change, per AGM), (4) Provenance Context (knowledge meaning SHALL include the provenance conditions under which it is valid, per provenance-enhanced KGs).

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a software platform for constructing, maintaining, investigating, evaluating, and acting upon governed knowledge states.
rows.statement: Positions KnowledgeOS as an 'Epistemic Operating System for AI and human engineering', explicitly not primarily a database, knowledge graph, RAG system, LLM, chatbot, agent framework, document-management system, workflow engine or rules engine (though it can use all of these); its product category answers 'how does an intelligent actor operate responsibly on knowledge when knowledge is incomplete, uncertain, conflicting, contextual and continuously changing?'.

rows.anchor: K_t \rightarrow Evaluate \rightarrow Gap/Conflict \rightarrow Investigate \rightarrow K_{t+1}
rows.statement: KnowledgeOS 'operates the knowledge lifecycle' rather than storing knowledge: Intent+Observation+Evidence -> Knowledge State -> Epistemic Navigation -> Decision/Action, iteratively K_t -> Evaluate -> Gap/Conflict -> Investigate -> K_{t+1}. Dimension Discovery is elevated to a first-class capability D_{t+1}=Discover(D_t,Q,O,K_t,C), letting KnowledgeOS operate below the level of explicit user specification — 'the Knower does not need to know the ontology in advance'.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS becomes an epistemic substrate for AI agents.
rows.statement: Contrasts a conventional agent loop (LLM->Tools->Action) with a KnowledgeOS-enabled agent that queries intent, current knowledge, supporting evidence, unknowns, conflicts, missing dimensions, next investigation, assumptions, Ideal State and discrepancy before acting — positioning KnowledgeOS as 'an epistemic substrate for AI agents', potentially its strongest product position. Also preserves the Observation->Assertion->Evidence->Inference->Hypothesis->Decision provenance chain for traceable reasoning, valuable for engineering/governance/compliance/safety-critical environments, and makes governance executable at the epistemic level (Knowledge->Evidence requirements->Epistemic rules->Validation->Decision eligibility->Action authorization), able to state 'this information exists but is not sufficiently evidenced for this decision'.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS \rightarrow \text{better structured epistemic conditions for reasoning and decision}
rows.statement: Explicit product boundaries: KnowledgeOS does not guarantee Knowledge=Truth, Inference=Truth, or Decision=Correct Decision; it makes uncertainty explicit and governable but cannot eliminate uncertainty from reality — KnowledgeOS -> 'better structured epistemic conditions for reasoning and decision'.

rows.anchor: Product category\n\nEpistemic Operating System
rows.statement: Final positioning: product category = Epistemic Operating System; product function = Knowledge State Management + Epistemic Navigation; enterprise positioning = Governed Knowledge Infrastructure for Humans and AI; AI positioning = Epistemic Runtime for AI Agents; engineering positioning = a system for evidence-backed, inspectable, continuously evolving engineering knowledge. Final loop: Intent->Knowledge State->Epistemic Evaluation->Investigation->Understanding->Decision->Action->Observation->Knowledge State', with Zero=epistemic diagnosis, Lord=epistemic horizon expansion, Sārathi=epistemic navigation, KnowledgeOS=the runtime coordinating the cycle — the point where KnowledgeOS 'stops being merely an AI platform and becomes a genuinely new product concept: an operating system for knowledge and epistemic work'.

rows.anchor: AI models become cognitive engines inside KnowledgeOS; KnowledgeOS becomes the epistemic operating environment in which those engines operate.
rows.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not replace the LLM but contain it: AI models become cognitive engines inside KnowledgeOS, which becomes the epistemic operating environment; AI Model ⊂ KnowledgeOS rather than KnowledgeOS = AI Model. Supplies a 20-row capability-mapping table translating current AI capabilities (RAG, summarization, classification, planning, tool use, memory, hallucination reduction, uncertainty, conflict handling, auditability, etc.) into KnowledgeOS capabilities (evidence-backed acquisition, knowledge transformation, Sārathi navigation, governed action execution, persistent Knowledge State, evidence/provenance/coherence controls, explicit epistemic state, conflict model, provenance+state history).

rows.anchor: Level 1 — KnowledgeOS + external AI
rows.statement: Proposes a three-level maturity roadmap: Level 1 KnowledgeOS + external AI (single external model, 'most realistic first implementation'); Level 2 KnowledgeOS + multiple models (model-agnostic, hosting OpenAI/Anthropic/local models simultaneously, KnowledgeOS 'governs how their outputs become knowledge'); Level 3 KnowledgeOS + own foundation models ('a complete independent AI platform').

rows.anchor: AI Capability \neq Epistemic Governance
rows.statement: Establishes as a fundamental architectural invariant: AI Capability ≠ Epistemic Governance, and KnowledgeOS = AI Capability + Knowledge State + Epistemic State + Evidence + Context + Governance + Navigation (provided AI capabilities are supplied by component models). KnowledgeOS's distinctive value is not generating better text than an LLM but providing 'the epistemic machinery around intelligence' — what the system knows, does not know, why it believes something, what conflicts, what is missing, what else might matter, whether it is justified in acting — which is why 'Epistemic Operating System' is kept as the product identity rather than 'another AI platform'.

rows.anchor: Foundation models are trained on large datasets. OpenAI describes three broad sources for its models: 1. publicly available information, 2. information obtained through third-party partnerships, 3. information provided or generated by users, human trainers, and researchers.
rows.statement: Cites OpenAI's own description of ChatGPT's information sources: (A) training-time learned parameters from public data, third-party partnerships, and user/trainer/researcher-provided data — the model is 'a learning machine, not a document database'; (B) inference-time retrieval (ChatGPT Search) that goes beyond built-in training knowledge and provides citations. Concludes mechanism (B) is much closer to what KnowledgeOS needs than (A).

Introduces a KnowledgeOS 'Source Plane' distinct from the 'Knowledge Plane', both feeding an Epistemic Engine (Zero/Lord/Sārathi): Source Plane answers 'where did this information come from?' (documents, APIs, git); Knowledge Plane answers 'what do we currently represent as knowledge?' (entities, assertions, dimensions, relations); Epistemic Engine answers 'how justified, complete, current and coherent is that knowledge?'. Proposes Source Connectors (file system, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, Markdown, Git, GitLab, GitHub, Confluence, SharePoint, Jira, Databases, REST APIs, Web, Email, enterprise repositories) as a first-class platform capability that must NOT simply dump content into a vector database but produce a controlled ingestion event.

rows.anchor: Path A — Model knowledge
rows.statement: Distinguishes three information pathways that must not be conflated: Path A Model knowledge (training data->foundation model->learned parameters->LLM response — implicit, non-traceable, non-governed); Path B External retrieval (sources->retrieval->evidence->KnowledgeOS — explicit, traceable, but ungoverned); Path C KnowledgeOS accumulated knowledge (observations+evidence+assertions+relationships+epistemic states+history->Knowledge State — explicit, traceable, governed, versioned, the only one that is 'the authoritative Knowledge State'). Worked example of a fully governed assertion record (Assertion A-10291: Subject/Dimension/Value/Evidence/Source/ObservedAt 2026-08-21/Acquisition/Support/Uncertainty/Validity/Provenance) illustrates Path C's K_t = 'explicit, versioned, traceable Knowledge State', something 'an LLM alone does not provide'.

rows.anchor: Source Fabric + Semantic Reconstruction + Knowledge State + Epistemic Engine + Investigation Engine + AI Models
rows.statement: Concludes KnowledgeOS should not be built as 'our own RAG' but as Source Fabric + Semantic Reconstruction + Knowledge State + Epistemic Engine + Investigation Engine + AI Models, making 'RAG merely one retrieval mechanism inside KnowledgeOS rather than the foundation of KnowledgeOS itself'. Final contrast: RAG asks 'what chunks are relevant to this question?'; KnowledgeOS asks 'what do we need to know, what do we know, what are the gaps, what evidence exists, and how should we investigate?' — KnowledgeOS is 'an epistemic investigation system, not a question-answering system'.

rows.anchor: Source Connectors are first-class citizens. They are not just "data loaders"; they are epistemic components that understand the provenance, reliability, and context of their sources.
rows.statement: A restating second-voice synthesis of the same material adds an implementation checklist: Source Connectors are epistemic components (not mere data loaders); Semantic Reconstruction is a core capability extracting structured observations/entities/dimensions/values (not just text); Candidate Assertions are held pending until evaluated (never auto-promoted to knowledge); Evidence Objects link observations to assertions with full provenance; Zero drives Retrieval (gaps become Sārathi investigation plans); LLMs are Tools, not the Knowledge State.

sources.note: The human author's own directive (quoted as 'the user has explicitly stated...') declining to resolve the two escalated normative questions (status vocabulary, K_t shape) from S1605, instead requiring exhaustive re-derivation first; introduces a Knowledge-State Requirements Register, a 7-way kernel-lineage reconciliation, 4 explicit status hypotheses (H1-H4, later vindicated in part by S1606), a 3-level minimality-confidence taxonomy, a 5-stage theory-to-implementation bridge, a 7-stage Theory Completion Gap Register, a mandatory 6-way result-category division, and a stricter 5-way exhaustion test before any user decision may be escalated.

rows.anchor: The user has explicitly stated that they do not know which alternative is mathematically or architecturally correct. Your responsibility now is to determine how much of these choices can still be derived ... Do NOT ask the user to choose between the alternatives yet.
rows.statement: Records the human author's actual response to the two questions S1605 escalated as AUTHOR INPUT REQUIRED (status vocabulary, K_t shape): the author declines to choose, states they do not know which alternative is correct, and instructs the verifier to first determine how much more can still be derived from the corpus/mathematics/statistics/computability/DDD/practical requirements before asking again -- a governance-significant act distinct from the verifier's own self-generated mandates elsewhere in this chain.

lineage_claims.quote: You have correctly identified that two questions currently appear normative: 1. the canonical epistemic-status vocabulary for Sigma; 2. the shape of the Knowledge State K_t.

rows.anchor: Construct a formal Knowledge-State Requirements Register. Derive every requirement from the historical corpus. [24 named capabilities] For every capability answer: [8 placement questions, including] Does putting it inside K create circularity? Does removing it from K lose information? Do not assume
rows.statement: Requires a Knowledge-State Requirements Register testing 24 named capabilities (assertion representation, epistemic status, evidence association, provenance, context, temporal validity, uncertainty, contradiction, missingness, unknown, identity, equality, membership, state transition, supersession, merge, replay, validation, authority, governance, lineage, determinism, composability, computability) against an 8-question placement test (property of K vs relation vs transformation vs history vs external assessment vs governance metadata vs circularity risk vs information loss on removal), explicitly rejecting the assumption that every KnowledgeOS requirement must be a K-component.

rows.anchor: Do not simply select one [kernel lineage]. Perform a semantic reconciliation. ... Determine whether apparently different primitives are: A. genuinely different concepts; B. aliases; C. different levels of abstraction; D. projections of one structure; E. historical alternatives; F. orthogonal dimensi
rows.statement: Requires reconciling the corpus's two competing kernel lineages via a 7-category relationship classification (genuinely different concepts / aliases / abstraction levels / projections of one structure / historical alternatives / orthogonal dimensions / incorrectly conflated concepts) applied to 18 named primitives, with an explicit ban on reconciling by chronology or assuming later definitions supersede earlier ones -- generalizing the anti-recency bias already voiced in S1605.

rows.anchor: Define K1 = K2 without accidentally making equality depend on: history; provenance; insertion order; event IDs; storage representation. Test whether the definition satisfies reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity.
rows.statement: Requires defining Knowledge-State equality with an explicit checklist of accidental dependencies to guard against (history, provenance, insertion order, event IDs, storage representation) and requires verifying the standard equivalence-relation properties (reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity) rather than assuming them.

rows.anchor: What is the smallest mathematical structure that satisfies all non-negotiable requirements? Construct a sequence K0 -> K1 -> K2 -> ... where each added component must have a demonstrated necessity. ... The final result must distinguish MINIMALITY PROVEN from MINIMALITY PLAUSIBLE from MINIMALITY NOT
rows.statement: Formalizes a 'minimal adequate K' procedure: build up a sequence K0->K1->K2->... adding only demonstrably-necessary components (tested against 7 questions per candidate: forcing requirement, external representability, derivability, removal breakage, reconstructability, circularity, unwanted coupling), and introduces a 3-level minimality-confidence taxonomy (PROVEN / PLAUSIBLE / NOT ESTABLISHED) explicitly rejecting fewer-fields as a minimality argument -- complementing S1608's congruence-based removal test with a positive constructive procedure.

rows.anchor: H1 -- One canonical finite status set ... H2 -- Status is multidimensional [EpistemicStatus vs GovernanceStatus, also evidential/validity/lifecycle/governance status] ... Determine whether the historical '11 competing vocabularies' are actually different dimensions that were incorrectly collapsed in
rows.statement: Poses 4 explicit, mutually-non-exclusive hypotheses to test regarding epistemic status (H1: one canonical finite set is mathematically required; H2: status is genuinely multidimensional, with the '11 competing vocabularies' possibly being distinct dimensions incorrectly collapsed into one field; H3: status is context-dependent, requiring a parameterized algebra; H4: status is partly derived rather than stored) -- H2 and H4 are exactly what S1606's subsequent analysis independently confirms.

rows.anchor: For every candidate status vocabulary, construct its transition relation: Sigma x Event -> Sigma ... Test: totality; determinism; reversibility where claimed; monotonicity where claimed; contradiction handling; supersession; invalidation; retraction; uncertainty; unknown. ... Which vocabulary permit
rows.statement: Requires evaluating each candidate status vocabulary by constructing its full transition relation (Sigma x Event -> Sigma) and testing 10 properties (totality, determinism, claimed reversibility, claimed monotonicity, contradiction handling, supersession, invalidation, retraction, uncertainty, unknown), converting the vocabulary-selection question into a mathematical criterion (fewest artificial exceptions) rather than a stylistic preference.

rows.anchor: observation != evidence; evidence != determination; determination != decision; decision != authorization; authorization != execution; validation != transformation; knowledge state != transformation history; provenance != lineage. ... If the mathematics collapses two DDD concepts into one object, rec
rows.statement: Lists 8 specific forbidden DDD conflations to test against the mathematics (observation!=evidence, evidence!=determination, determination!=decision, decision!=authorization, authorization!=execution, validation!=transformation, knowledge-state!=transformation-history, provenance!=lineage), requiring that any point where the formal model collapses two of these be recorded as a contradiction rather than silently accepted.

rows.anchor: Construct: Mathematical Object -> KnowledgeOS Concept -> Data Structure -> Operation -> Test. ... Do not invent implementation details merely to make the mapping work. If no implementation mapping exists, classify the concept as: THEORETICALLY DEFINED / IMPLEMENTATION MISSING.
rows.statement: Requires a 5-stage implementation-bridge chain (Mathematical Object -> KnowledgeOS Concept -> Data Structure -> Operation -> Test) for every proposed theory object, with an explicit fallback classification (THEORETICALLY DEFINED / IMPLEMENTATION MISSING) rather than inventing implementation details to force the mapping to close.

rows.anchor: Reject any numerical uncertainty claim that lacks a valid statistical basis. Distinguish: epistemic uncertainty; aleatory uncertainty; missingness; non-identifiability; contradiction; ignorance/unknown. Do not let a probability number become a substitute for these distinct concepts.
rows.statement: Mandates a statistical audit rejecting any numerical uncertainty claim lacking a valid statistical basis (random variable, sample space, estimand, observation model, probability space, conditioning information, estimator, calibration semantics, uncertainty interpretation all specified), and requires distinguishing 6 named concepts (epistemic uncertainty, aleatory uncertainty, missingness, non-identifiability, contradiction, ignorance/unknown) that a bare probability number must never be allowed to substitute for.

rows.anchor: Create a Theory Completion Gap Register. [pipeline: Historical Corpus -> Conceptual Theory -> Formal Theory -> Computable Theory -> KnowledgeOS Model -> Executable Implementation -> Empirical Validation] Each gap must have: GAP-ID, Question, Why it matters, Evidence, Current status, Blocking?, Can b
rows.statement: Requires a Theory Completion Gap Register mapping gaps across a 7-stage pipeline (Historical Corpus -> Conceptual Theory -> Formal Theory -> Computable Theory -> KnowledgeOS Model -> Executable Implementation -> Empirical Validation), each gap carrying an 11-field record (GAP-ID through Resolution path) -- the most granular gap-tracking schema introduced in this batch's mandate chain.

rows.anchor: Do not attempt to 'complete the theory' by silently inserting engineering preferences. Explicitly divide results into: Mathematical necessities; Empirical facts; Historical facts; Architectural consequences; Design choices; User/business/governance decisions. This separation is mandatory.
rows.statement: Mandates a strict 6-way mandatory division of every result (mathematical necessity, empirical fact, historical fact, architectural consequence, design choice, or user/business/governance decision), explicitly forbidding silently inserting engineering preferences as if they were mathematical necessities -- a finer-grained successor to the earlier A/B/C/D evidence-class scheme (S1596).

rows.anchor: Only include decisions for which: the corpus does not determine the answer; mathematics does not determine the answer; DDD semantics does not determine the answer; implementation requirements do not determine the answer; empirical testing cannot determine the answer. ... rows.statement: Sharpens the S1604 author-escalation protocol into a stricter 5-way exhaustion test (corpus, mathematics, DDD semantics, implementation requirements, and empirical testing must ALL fail to determine an answer) before a question may be classified as a genuinely irreducible user decision -- explicitly forbidding escalation merely because the corpus contains competing alternatives (exactly the mistake S1606 later shows the verifier made with the status vocabulary).

rows.anchor: Do not use: 'verified'; 'complete'; 'canonical'; 'minimal'; 'correct'; 'production-ready' unless the corresponding proof/evidence exists. ... rows.statement: Bans 6 specific completion-claiming words (verified, complete, canonical, minimal, correct, production-ready) unless matching proof/evidence exists, and defines the actual completion criterion as an independent-reconstruction test: a senior mathematician, statistician, DDD architect and software architect must each be able to reconstruct the theory from the final specification, compute every operation, identify every assumption, reproduce every result, and separate proven theory from design choice and hypothesis.

rows.statement: States the guiding restraint: we should not assume knowledge forms a lattice merely because lattices are useful in distributed systems -- the structure must be derived from semantics. A conventional database's Fact=True/False is insufficient; KnowledgeOS needs at least True, False, Unknown, and potentially Uncertain, Contradictory -- KnowledgeState != BooleanState.

rows.anchor: E(p) epistemic assessment domain; Support != Truth
rows.statement: Defines E(p) as the epistemic assessment of proposition p, minimally E(p) in {Unknown, Supported, Validated, Contradicted}, but insufficient alone. Restates Support != Truth: Evidence(E1)|=p gives Supported(p) but does not mathematically establish Truth(p)=True -- 'one of the foundational principles'.

rows.anchor: Evidence aggregation preserves competing support; Conflict(p) = Support(p)>0 ∧ Support(¬p)>0 as genuine epistemic disagreement
rows.statement: When E1,E2|=p and E3|=not-p, KnowledgeOS must preserve the competing evidence for p and not-p. Defines Conflict(p) = Support(p)>0 ∧ Support(not-p)>0, explicitly not necessarily a system error but potentially 'genuine epistemic disagreement'.

rows.anchor: Contradiction, Uncertainty, and Ignorance are three non-collapsible concepts
rows.statement: Distinguishes Ignorance (Evidence(p)=empty, leading to Unknown(p)) from Uncertainty (information exists but does not strongly determine the proposition, e.g. P(p)=0.65, so Unknown != Uncertain) from Contradiction (evidence supports competing propositions, P(supports p)>0 and P(supports not-p)>0, so Contradiction != Uncertainty). These three must not collapse into one state.
invariants: Ignorance, Uncertainty, and Contradiction are three distinct epistemic states, never collapsed into one

rows.anchor: Two-dimensional epistemic state K(p)=(Support+,Support-,Uncertainty,Provenance); not automatically probabilities
rows.statement: Represents K(p) = (Support+(p), Support-(p), Uncertainty, Provenance), arguing a single scalar confidence cannot cleanly distinguish strong asymmetrical support (Support+=0.8, Support-=0.1) from strong disagreement (Support+=0.8, Support-=0.8). Warns S+, S- in [0,1] must not automatically be interpreted as P(p) and P(not-p) -- they become probabilities only if statistical semantics justify it; if a probabilistic model P(p|E) is explicitly defined, P(not-p|E)=1-P(p|E) for a binary exhaustive proposition, but generic support scores need not obey that equation. Separates an Epistemic layer (Support, Conflict, Provenance) from a Statistical layer (Probability, Likelihood, Posterior) that interact but are not identical.
invariants: support scores S+/S- are not automatically probabilities; they become probabilities only under an explicit justified statistical model

rows.anchor: Knowledge state as a claim set with subset-based partial order; TruthOrdering != InformationOrdering; ProbabilityOrder != InformationOrder
rows.statement: Represents K={c1,...,cn} (claims plus epistemic metadata) with a natural candidate ordering K_A ⪯ K_B if Claims(K_A) subset-of Claims(K_B) and existing claims retain compatible semantics -- but notes K_A={p} subset-of K_B={p,not-p} introduces contradiction, so whether K_B represents 'more knowledge' depends on epistemic semantics, motivating a distinction between TruthOrdering and InformationOrdering (a state with more information is not necessarily a state with more truth). Defines an informal information order K_A ⊑ K_B (K_B has at least as much relevant information), e.g. Unknown ⊑ Supported(p), with Supported(p) ⊑ Supported(p)+ContradictoryEvidence requiring domain choice. Warns a probability change (0.6->0.9) does not necessarily mean more information, just a changed estimate -- ProbabilityOrder != InformationOrder.

rows.anchor: Merge != Resolve as distinct domain operations; nine merge/resolution experiments (all PASS) including historical-conflict preservation
rows.statement: Defines Merge(K_A,K_B)=K_M as potentially containing Conflict(p) -- Merge != Resolve; Resolution is a separate operation using AdditionalEvidence, DomainPolicy, HumanAdjudication, or a StatisticalModel: Resolve(K_M,E) -> K_R, kept as distinct DDD operations rather than one generic updateKnowledge(). Experiment 1: disjoint K_A={p}, K_B={q} merge without conflict to {p,q} -- PASS. Experiment 2: duplicate claims K_A={p}, K_B={p} require identity/deduplication semantics rather than creating two identical claims -- PASS given explicit claim-identity/proposition-equivalence definitions. Experiment 3: K_A={p}, K_B={not-p} merge to K_M={p,not-p} yielding Conflict(p) -- PASS. Experiment 4: attempting Resolve(K_M,p) without additional evidence or policy is Rejected -- PASS. Experiment 5: new evidence E4 strongly supporting p allows Resolve(K_M,E4)->K_R where p becomes dominant/validated per policy, with the original conflict remaining historically visible -- PASS, giving a temporal property: Conflict(p) does not disappear from history even after resolution, instead ConflictAt(t1) followed by ResolvedAt(t2).
invariants: Merge ≠ Resolve: merging never implicitly resolves a conflict
a resolved conflict remains historically visible (ConflictAt(t1) → ResolvedAt(t2)), never erased

experiment.hypothesis: Merge and Resolve behave as distinct operations: merge preserves conflict rather than silently resolving it, and resolution requires justification (evidence/policy) while retaining historical visibility of the original conflict.
experiment.assumptions: Claim identity and proposition-equivalence semantics are assumed explicitly defined where needed.
experiment.inputs: Five scenario premises as summarized in the statement.
experiment.method: Construct each merge/resolution scenario and check the resulting knowledge state against the expected outcome.
experiment.interpretation: Merge and Resolve are genuinely distinct domain operations; conflict resolution requires justification and never erases historical conflict.
experiment.limitations: Manual scenario reasoning, not automated/exhaustive verification.

rows.anchor: Knowledge version graph G_K=(V,E); RevisionGraph != CausalGraph; candidate partial order tested for reflexivity/antisymmetry/transitivity
rows.statement: Represents legitimate branching K1->K2^A and K1->K2^B (competing hypotheses) as a version graph G_K=(V,E) with V=KnowledgeStates and E=RevisionRelations, more general than a simple version chain; argues a revision graph should normally be acyclic (a revision should not causally depend on itself) while a domain may separately represent cyclic feedback elsewhere, distinguishing RevisionGraph from CausalGraph. Defines the candidate partial order K_A⪯K_B (K_B is a valid successor/refinement of K_A) and tests it for reflexivity (K_A⪯K_A), antisymmetry (K_A⪯K_B ∧ K_B⪯K_A ⇒ K_A=K_B under the chosen equivalence), and transitivity (K_A⪯K_B ∧ K_B⪯K_C ⇒ K_A⪯K_C).

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS cannot yet be declared a lattice: Join may not exist under a consistency requirement
rows.statement: Notes a lattice requires every pair K_A,K_B to have Meet(K_A,K_B) and Join(K_A,K_B), which 'we cannot yet claim'. Example: K_A={p}, K_B={not-p} give a candidate join {p,not-p} under set inclusion, but if a knowledge state requires consistency the union is not admissible, so Join may not exist within the consistent subset -- 'KnowledgeOS cannot yet be declared a lattice. This is exactly the kind of mathematical restraint we want.'

rows.anchor: Semilattice properties (commutativity, idempotence, associativity) proven for pure set-union merge only, not for the full semantic merge
rows.statement: Tests, for the basic set-union representation only, three semilattice properties: commutativity Merge(A,B)=Merge(B,A) (A∪B=B∪A) -- PASS; idempotence Merge(A,A)=A (A∪A=A) -- PASS; associativity Merge(Merge(A,B),C)=Merge(A,Merge(B,C)) ((A∪B)∪C=A∪(B∪C)) -- PASS. But explicitly qualifies this holds only for PureClaimSetUnion; the full KnowledgeOS semantic merge additionally involves supersession, temporal validity, contradiction, confidence, provenance, semantic equivalence, and policy, so the real merge operator may not satisfy the semilattice laws -- 'we cannot yet assert KnowledgeOS is a semilattice.'

experiment.hypothesis: Pure set-union merge of claim sets satisfies the semilattice laws (commutativity, idempotence, associativity).
experiment.setup: Three algebraic-property tests (60.39-60.41) on the basic set-union model.
experiment.assumptions: Merge is modeled as plain set union with no temporal/supersession/probabilistic semantics.
experiment.inputs: Symbolic claim sets A, B, C.
experiment.method: Check each semilattice law against set-union algebra.
experiment.result: All three properties PASS for pure set union.
experiment.interpretation: The pure-set-union fragment of merge is a genuine (join-)semilattice, but this does not extend to the full semantic merge operator, which remains unproven.
experiment.limitations: Applies only to the simplified pure-set-union model, explicitly not the full KnowledgeOS merge semantics.
experiment.conclusion: Semilattice properties PASS for pure set union; full semantic merge remains an open question.

rows.anchor: Version-aware merge for supersession; temporal-scope-bounded contradiction Conflict(p,t)
rows.statement: Experiment: K_A has p-version-1, K_B has p-version-2; a naive union produces both, but p_2 may semantically supersede p_1, requiring a version-aware Merge_v(K_A,K_B) that retains both historical states while defining Active(p)=p_2 -- not ordinary set union. Experiment: p valid during [0,10] and not-p valid during [10,20] do not conflict since the intervals do not overlap, so contradiction must be temporal: Conflict(p) is required only when competing claims overlap in the relevant semantic scope -- Conflict(p,t), with TemporalScope as part of epistemic reasoning.

rows.anchor: Typed proposition identity prevents naive scope conflation; ClaimIdentity != TextIdentity; semantic similarity is another epistemic firewall instance
rows.statement: Experiment: p_A ('SystemA is Healthy') and p_B ('SystemB is Unhealthy') are not contradictory despite superficial similarity -- a naive string comparison could incorrectly infer conflict, so PropositionEquality must consider Subject, Predicate, Object, Scope, and potentially Time. Notes semantically equivalent but syntactically different propositions ('SystemA is healthy' vs 'SystemA hasStatus Healthy') require explicit SemanticMapping, never assumed string equality -- giving ClaimIdentity != TextIdentity, essential for AI-generated knowledge. Experiment: two agents' differently-phrased claims may remain Unknown as to equivalence unless the semantic-normalization mapping is sufficiently reliable -- PASS, restated as another epistemic firewall instance: AI semantic similarity must not automatically become Identity; similarity is evidence for equivalence, not equivalence itself.
invariants: semantic similarity between AI-generated claims is evidence for equivalence, never automatically identity

lineage_claims.quote: This is another epistemic firewall.

rows.anchor: Five-stage knowledge-merge pipeline; contrast with RAG's plain-text combination
rows.statement: Defines a rigorous merge pipeline: K_A,K_B -> CandidateAlignment -> SemanticValidation -> Merge -> ConflictDetection -> Resolution if applicable -- contrasted with RAG, which generally just combines retrieved text; KnowledgeOS instead combines StructuredPropositions + Evidence + Semantics + TemporalScope.

rows.anchor: Full Bayesian-update worked example via likelihood ratios; posterior != truth, != confidence
rows.statement: Worked example: prior P(p)=0.5 (odds O(p)=1), evidence E with likelihood ratio LR=P(E|p)/P(E|not-p)=4, posterior odds O(p|E)=O(p)*LR=4, posterior P(p|E)=4/(1+4)=0.8. Explicitly warns P(p|E)=0.8 means only that, under the specified probabilistic model -- it does not mean Truth(p)=0.8 and does not automatically mean Confidence=0.8. If the domain supports Bayesian inference as a first-class operation UpdateBelief(P,E)->P', the result should record Prior, Evidence, LikelihoodModel, Posterior, ModelVersion, giving Bayesian provenance P -> E -> LikelihoodModel -> P' consistent with the general provenance architecture.
invariants: a Bayesian posterior probability is never equated with Truth(p) or with a separate Confidence score

rows.anchor: Conflicting-evidence Bayesian example (LR returns to 1.0); evidence independence required; EvidenceCount != EvidenceStrength (duplicate-evidence non-double-counting)
rows.statement: Worked example: P(p)=0.5, E1 gives LR1=4 (P(p|E1)=0.8), E2 gives LR2=0.25, combined LR=4*0.25=1, so P(p|E1,E2)=0.5 -- illustrating conflicting evidence returning the posterior toward the prior without discarding either evidence -- PASS. Warns the multiplication LR1*LR2 assumes appropriate conditional independence, which must be recorded, not blindly assumed; if E1 and E2 share an underlying source, treating them as independent overstates evidence (EvidenceDependency). States the major statistical requirement EvidenceCount != EvidenceStrength: 'ten copies of the same report are not necessarily ten independent pieces of evidence'. Experiment: E1=E2=E, naive multiplication would incorrectly give LR^2, but the provenance/dependency model identifies E1≡E2 so evidence is not double-counted -- PASS given available dependency identity, distinguishing MoreDocuments from MoreIndependentEvidence.
invariants: EvidenceCount ≠ EvidenceStrength: duplicate or dependent evidence must never be double-counted as independent confirmation

lineage_claims.quote: Ten copies of the same report are not necessarily ten independent pieces of evidence.

rows.anchor: Seven-field Claim=(P,E,S,T,U,V,M) object; Claim != Text; knowledge graph G_K=(C,R) with typed epistemic edges
rows.statement: Consolidates the claim object as C=(P,E,S,T,U,V,M): Proposition, Evidence/provenance, epistemic Status, Temporal scope, Uncertainty, Version, semantic (M)eaning/context -- 'becoming the central knowledge object'. States a KnowledgeOS Claim is not merely a sentence but a structured epistemic object: Claim != Text. The complete knowledge state K={C1,...,Cn} plus relations R(K) and provenance Prov(K) forms a knowledge graph G_K=(C,R) with typed edges (Supports, Contradicts, DerivedFrom, Supersedes, Refines, DependsOn) -- noting not every relation is epistemic (e.g. Causes belongs to causal semantics), so the knowledge graph may contain typed relations from multiple contexts while ownership remains context-specific.

lineage_claims.quote: A KnowledgeOS Claim is therefore not merely a sentence. It is a structured epistemic object.

rows.anchor: Central finding: KnowledgeOS knowledge is a versioned, provenance-aware, temporally-scoped, partially ordered collection of structured propositions; lattice status left open
rows.statement: States the Step 60 central finding: KnowledgeOS knowledge is a versioned, provenance-aware, temporally-scoped, partially ordered collection of structured propositions -- 'a much stronger statement than KnowledgeOS stores knowledge'. Confirms the basic set-union representation has semilattice properties (commutative, associative, idempotent), but the full semantic merge (contradiction, temporal validity, supersession, semantic equivalence, probabilistic updates, provenance, policy) means KnowledgeOS cannot yet be asserted to be a semilattice; lattice structure remains an open hypothesis.

rows.anchor: Operational State vs Epistemic State architectural split
rows.statement: Introduces the architecture's two fundamentally different state spaces: Operational state (wants controlled authoritative transitions: Decision/Action -> Authorization -> Execution -> Outcome) and Epistemic state (may legitimately branch, conflict, merge, and revise: Claims/Hypotheses -> Evidence/Support -> Conflict/Merge -> Revision/Learning), both feeding into Governance -- 'this distinction is extremely important' and 'a significant refinement'.

lineage_claims.quote: The architecture now has two fundamentally different state spaces.

rows.anchor: Step 60 verdict PASS WITH A MATHEMATICAL QUALIFICATION; opens Step 61 on information gain, uncertainty and epistemic quality
rows.statement: Declares STEP 60 -- PASS WITH A MATHEMATICAL QUALIFICATION: KnowledgeState, KnowledgeMerge, Conflict, Uncertainty, TemporalScope, Provenance, and BayesianUpdate were successfully derived without collapsing them into one concept, but lattice structure remains an open hypothesis. Opens Step 61 (Information Gain, Uncertainty and Epistemic Quality): can KnowledgeOS mathematically quantify what was learned (e.g. P(p): 0.5->0.8, was InformationGain>0, how much), accounting for correlated evidence and worsening calibration despite more extreme probability, with the central question of whether KnowledgeOS can distinguish 'more confident' from 'actually better informed' -- framed as crucial for KnowledgeOS to become 'the mathematical knowledge substrate for AI engineering, rather than simply another AI/RAG storage system'.

rows.anchor: Epistemic quality is generally a partial order, not a single number; Pareto incomparability among knowledge states
rows.statement: Defines Delta EQ = EQ(K_{t+1}) - EQ(K_t), noting this is not automatically a scalar since EQ is multidimensional; example where Uncertainty decreases but ProvenanceQuality decreases has no universal 'improved or not' answer -- 'EpistemicQuality is generally a partial order, not necessarily a single number... an important mathematical finding'. Gives a Pareto interpretation: K_B succ K_A only if K_B is at least as good in all relevant dimensions and strictly better in one; otherwise the states may be incomparable, illustrated by a four-dimension table (evidence strength, freshness, independence, uncertainty) where neither K_A nor K_B dominates, giving K_A parallel K_B. Experiment: attempting K_A>K_B with no dominance relation correctly yields Incomparable -- PASS, refining the earlier K_A⪯K_B hypothesis toward MoreInformative subject to Reliability/Independence/Freshness/Validity rather than MoreClaims=Better.

lineage_claims.target: kos-epistemic-algebra's candidate knowledge partial order K_A⪯K_B (Step 60)
lineage_claims.quote: This connects to our earlier partial-order hypothesis... Step 61 gives this idea more substance.

rows.anchor: Epistemic merge as a domain-specific operation, never a generic infrastructure function (generic-merge experiment FAILs)
rows.statement: Defines merge M(S_A,S_B): for independent artifacts M=S_A union S_B; for conflicting claims M=S_merged+Conflict (never OneWinner). Experiment 6: A and B independently producing contradictory claims yields a MergedState containing Claim_A, Claim_B, and a ConflictRecord -- PASS. Contrasts with Git-style text merging ('can these modifications coexist') versus KnowledgeOS's semantic question ('what is the epistemic relationship'). States merge must be a domain (bounded-context) operation, not one generic infrastructure function -- EvidenceContext and DecisionContext may have different merge semantics. Experiment 7: using one universal merge algorithm across evidence/claims/policies/authorizations yields ArchitecturalFailure -- explicitly FAIL, 'the semantics differ too much'.

lineage_claims.quote: Merge is therefore a domain operation.

experiment.hypothesis: A single universal merge algorithm cannot correctly handle evidence, claims, policies, and authorizations simultaneously.
experiment.setup: Experiment 7 (72.17): applying one generic merge function across all four artifact kinds.
experiment.assumptions: Each bounded context has its own legitimate merge semantics.
experiment.inputs: Evidence, claims, policies, authorizations under one generic merge().
experiment.method: Evaluate whether one merge algorithm produces correct results across all four semantic domains.
experiment.interpretation: Merge must be a bounded-context-owned domain operation, never a generic infrastructure function.
experiment.limitations: A design-level judgment rather than a runnable test.

lexical.anchor: KnowledgeState != BooleanState; deriving structure from semantics rather than assuming a lattice

formal.anchor: E(p) epistemic assessment domain; Support != Truth

rationale_evidence.anchor: KnowledgeOS cannot yet be declared a lattice: Join may not exist under a consistency requirement
rationale_evidence.statement: Notes a lattice requires every pair K_A,K_B to have Meet(K_A,K_B) and Join(K_A,K_B), which 'we cannot yet claim'. Example: K_A={p}, K_B={not-p} give a candidate join {p,not-p} under set inclusion, but if a knowledge state requires consistency the union is not admissible, so Join may not exist within the consistent subset -- 'KnowledgeOS cannot yet be declared a lattice. This is exactly the kind of mathematical restraint we want.'

notations: Σ_0 (10 values) = flattening of the product

sources.note: Findings (attributed to 'Q4A' and research steps F3/F4) that the older 10-value Sigma_0 status vocabulary is a flattening of a corpus five-axis product structure Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C), with a proposed (DERIVED, not ratified) repair replacing the S component with a polarity powerset P({Support,Refute}), and a projection-based observational equality Sigma_1 approx_X Sigma_2 reducing the equality governance question to choosing among 32 candidate axis-subsets X.

rows.anchor: | `Σ` epistemic state | 🟢 substantially recovered | Q4A establishes the 5-axis product and componentwise transitions | | 10-value `Σ₀` | 🟢 explained | It is a flattening; 7 values map to the product, 3 are not epistemic status |
rows.statement: Reports that the older 10-value Sigma_0 status vocabulary is now explained as a flattening of the newly-recovered 5-axis product structure (A,S,R,V,C): 7 of its values map onto the product structure, while 3 are not epistemic status at all.

rows.anchor: F3's repair of `(A,S,R,V,C)` should **not be promoted to architecture**. The chain is: `Q4A` → establishes five-axis structure `272B` → establishes polarity powerset for Support/Refute **research composition** → proposes replacing `S` with `P({Sup,Ref})` That last arrow is **DERIVED**, not corpus-native and not ratified.
rows.statement: Traces the provenance of a proposed repair (F3) to the five-axis Sigma structure: Q4A established the five-axis structure itself, corpus step 272B independently established a polarity powerset for Support/Refute, and a research composition proposes replacing the S component with P({Support,Refute}) — but this last composing step is explicitly DERIVED (research-constructed), not corpus-native or ratified, and must not be promoted to architecture.

rows.anchor: $$ \Sigma_1\approx_X\Sigma_2 \iff \pi_X(\Sigma_1)=\pi_X(\Sigma_2) $$ is a very useful reduction, but it does **not** choose which `X` KnowledgeOS should adopt. The research has reduced the governance question from "invent an observational equality" to "choose among a bounded family of projections."
rows.statement: Reports finding F4: observational equality parameterised as Sigma_1 approx_X Sigma_2 iff their projections onto axis-subset X agree — a useful reduction of the governance question from 'invent an observational equality' to 'choose among a bounded family of projections' (32 candidate axis-subsets), but it does not itself choose X, so remains normative/governance-pending.
missing: which axis-subset X KnowledgeOS should adopt

rows.anchor: | **A** — Acquisition | Observed, Reported, Inferred, Calculated, Assumed, Hypothesized, Unknown | 7 | | **S** — Support | None, Weak, Moderate, Strong, Very Strong | 5 | | **R** — Resolution | Open, In Progress, Resolved, Unresolvable | 4 | | **V** — Validity | Current, Stale, Expired, Unknown | 4 | | **C** — Conflict | None, Potential, Active, Resolved | 4 | **State space: \( 7 \times 5 \times 4 \times 4 \times 4 = 2240 \)**
rows.statement: Confirms the exact five-axis product Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) recovered from corpus source Q4A (dated 20260826-173318): A/Acquisition (7 values: Observed, Reported, Inferred, Calculated, Assumed, Hypothesized, Unknown), S/Support (5: None, Weak, Moderate, Strong, Very Strong), R/Resolution (4: Open, In Progress, Resolved, Unresolvable), V/Validity (4: Current, Stale, Expired, Unknown), C/Conflict (4: None, Potential, Active, Resolved), giving a total state space of 7x5x4x4x4=2240, with componentwise transition functions Sigma_new=T(Sigma_old,E) applying T_A,T_S,T_R,T_V,T_C independently, recovered within hours of the original gap being raised.

rows.anchor: | `Satisfied` | **S** = Strong/Very Strong | ✅ Mapped | ... | `NotApplicable` | 🔴 No axis | **Scope predicate** | `Prohibited` | 🔴 No axis | **Policy verdict** | `Missing` | 🔴 No axis | **Inquiry layer (`Q_t`)** | **7 of 10 map onto the five axes. Three do not.**
rows.statement: Maps the older 10-value status set (from corpus doc 025d) onto the five-axis product: Satisfied->S=Strong/VeryStrong, PartiallySatisfied->S=Moderate, Unknown->A=Unknown OR S=None (flagged as two different senses of Unknown), Insufficient->S=None/Weak, Conflicted->C=Active, Stale->V=Stale, Invalid->V=Expired(approx) — all mapped; while NotApplicable (a scope predicate), Prohibited (a policy verdict), and Missing (belongs to the inquiry layer Q_t/D_t) have no axis at all and are not epistemic-status values.

rows.anchor: $$ \Sigma_0 = \mathcal{P}(\{\text{Support}, \text{Refute}\}) \cong \{0,1\}^2 $$ ... $$ \boxed{ \Sigma = \big(A,\; \mathcal{P}(\{\text{Sup},\text{Ref}\}),\; R,\; V,\; C\big) } $$ ... Each source repairs the other's exact defect. **State space becomes \( 7 \times 4 \times 4 \times 4 \times 4 = 1792 \).**
rows.statement: Confirms the repair for the refuted single-polarity Support axis (which could not express 'the evidence refutes this'): corpus Step 272B independently supplies a polarity powerset Sigma_0=P({Support,Refute})≅{0,1}^2, and composing it into the five-axis product gives Sigma=(A, P({Sup,Ref}), R, V, C) with state space 7x4x4x4x4=1792 — each source repairs exactly the other's defect, but the composition itself is graded DERIVED, not CORPUS, since neither source document proposes it; not promoted, but resolves a recorded refutation using only corpus material.

rows.anchor: $$ \Sigma_1 \approx_X \Sigma_2 \iff \pi_X(\Sigma_1) = \pi_X(\Sigma_2), \quad X \subseteq \{A, S, R, V, C\} $$ **The axes ARE the permitted observations.** $$ 2^5 = 32 \text{ candidate relations} $$
rows.statement: Confirms the derivation that with a product state space, observational equality naturally becomes projection onto an axis subset X (Sigma_1 approx_X Sigma_2 iff pi_X(Sigma_1)=pi_X(Sigma_2)), so the axes themselves ARE the permitted observations — giving exactly 2^5=32 candidate relations forming a natural containment lattice (from ≈_∅, everything equal, to ≈_{A,S,R,V,C}, structural equality on Sigma); changes the target's status from an undefined normative parameter to a form-DERIVED relation with a bounded 32-option normative choice remaining.

rows.anchor: $$ \Sigma_1 \preceq \Sigma_2 \iff A_1 \preceq_A A_2 \wedge S_1 \preceq_S S_2 \wedge R_1 \preceq_R R_2 \wedge V_1 \preceq_V V_2 \wedge C_1 \preceq_C C_2 $$ **It is a partial order by construction and NOT total.** ... `Observed` and `Conflicting` sit on **different axes**, so they are **incomparable**, not mis-ordered.
rows.statement: Confirms the derivation of a product partial order for K_{t+1}≻K_t as a componentwise conjunction of five per-axis orders, resolving an earlier objection ('Observed ≮ Conflicting in any obvious scalar sense') by noting Observed and Conflicting sit on different axes and are therefore incomparable rather than mis-ordered; caveats: each per-axis order must itself still be declared (Acquisition A has no obvious order), the product gives a lattice only if every component is a lattice, and 'more knowledge' is not the same claim as 'higher Sigma'.
missing: declared per-axis orders, especially for A

rows.anchor: In `Σ=(A,S,R,V,C)`: | "No information about how it was obtained" | **A** = Unknown | | "Validity unknown" | **V** = Unknown | | "No evidence" | **S** = None | **Three different senses of not-knowing, two sharing one label.** ... The mathematical review proposed `Σ_O` for selection/projection — **which collided with Q4A's `Σ` for epistemic state, written 51 minutes later.**
rows.statement: Confirms two notation collisions: 'Unknown' is overloaded across three distinct senses (A=Unknown: no information about acquisition; V=Unknown: validity unknown; S=None: no evidence — with A and V sharing one label for two different senses), and the symbol Sigma itself collided (a mathematical review proposed Sigma_O for selection/projection, colliding with Q4A's Sigma for epistemic state written only 51 minutes later); neither S nor Sigma was ever disambiguated in the corpus.

rows.anchor: `Σ` is currently treated as derived rather than canonical stored state; the corpus provides the five-axis state construction and transition algebra, while storage semantics remain an architectural question. ... the statement `Σ is never stored` is an architectural storage decision, not merely a mathematical consequence.
rows.statement: Corrects the claim 'Sigma derived, never stored (proven: OR-merge incompatible with retract)' by separating two claims at different evidential levels: the OR-merge/retract incompatibility proof establishes a constraint on one proposed storage representation, not the universal proposition 'Sigma can never be stored' -- storage semantics for Sigma remain an open architectural question, not a settled mathematical consequence.

rows.anchor: **Notation status:** `Σ` is used here for the Q4A five-axis epistemic state. Earlier corpus material uses `Σ_O` for observation selection and `S` for multiple concepts. These collisions are recorded in the UL/notation reconciliation and are not resolved by Step 285.
rows.statement: Recommends adding an explicit notation-status disclaimer to Step 285 warning that its use of Sigma for the Q4A five-axis epistemic state collides with earlier corpus usage (Sigma_O for observation selection, S for multiple concepts), unresolved by Step 285 itself, so that Step 286 (the ontology step) does not silently inherit an unresolved symbol collision.

rows.anchor: the sentence "the axes ARE the observations" is slightly stronger than the evidence supports. I'd change it to: **"For the state-level `Σ` model, the axes provide a bounded candidate space for permitted observations."** Then: **"Selecting the actual observation subset `X` remains normative."**
rows.statement: Tightens the ≈_X derivation: 'the axes ARE the observations' is stronger than established; the corrected claim is that the five axes provide a bounded candidate space for permitted observations, while selecting the actual observation subset X remains a separate normative decision -- distinguishes the mathematical derivation (observational equality over Sigma is representable as axis-subset projection) from the architectural claim (KnowledgeOS's permitted observations ARE exactly subsets of {A,S,R,V,C}), only the former being established.

rows.anchor: **"A product partial-order structure is available as a mathematical construction; the KnowledgeOS order itself remains under-specified until the component orders are declared."** ... What has been established is the **candidate mathematical structure**.
rows.statement: Distinguishes the mathematical fact (five component partial orders compose into a Cartesian-product partial order) from the architectural claim (KnowledgeOS's actual K_{t+1}≻K_t order has been formally established) -- the corpus has not yet supplied the five component orders (especially Acquisition), so only the candidate mathematical structure exists, not an established KnowledgeOS order.

sources.note: A research hypothesis modeling two orthogonal knowledge dimensions (e.g. semantic state and authority state, or confidence and trust) as the real/imaginary parts of a complex number, extended to a difference operator and a five-dimensional vector generalization; explicitly not to be equated with 'knowledge' itself.

rows.anchor: K = S + iA where S = semantic state, A = authority state ... What something says and whether the organization is authorized to treat it as true are different dimensions.
rows.statement: Proposes representing a knowledge artifact's semantic-state and authority-state as the real and imaginary components of a complex number, so the two dimensions are never collapsed into a single scalar.

rows.anchor: ΔK = ΔS + iΔA ... They disagree semantically. from: They agree semantically, but their authority states conflict. Those are completely different governance problems.
rows.statement: Extends the complex-number model with a difference operator separating semantic conflict from authority conflict as two distinct governance problems, noting compatibility with the existing R-CONFLICT concept.

lineage_claims.quote: This is actually very compatible with the R-CONFLICT thinking we've already developed.

rows.anchor: Do not make 'complex number = knowledge' ... KnowledgeOS is fundamentally about: meaning, evidence, provenance, authority, lifecycle, invariants, relationships, decisions, governance. A complex number cannot represent all of that.
rows.statement: Explicitly warns against equating knowledge itself with a complex number; mathematics is proposed as a domain-supporting analytical mechanism layered above the domain model, never the domain model itself.

rows.anchor: K = [S, E, A, P, T]^T ... complex numbers become a special two-dimensional projection: z = S+iA or z = E+iP.
rows.statement: Generalizes the two-dimensional complex-number model into a five-dimensional vector (semantic validity, evidence strength, authority, provenance integrity, temporal validity), with any complex-number model recast as a special two-axis projection of the fuller vector.
missing: a derivation of which axis pairs are architecturally meaningful

rows.anchor: EKS PKS AIP → Current architecture → Domain discovery → Invariants → Knowledge concepts → Mathematical properties → Mathematical representation. Not: Complex numbers → invent KnowledgeOS model.
rows.statement: States a DDD-priority ordering rule: mathematical representation must be derived last, after current-architecture evidence, domain discovery, invariants, and knowledge concepts are established — never chosen first and used to invent the domain model.

rows.anchor: I would record this as a research hypothesis, not an architecture decision ... Can the semantic state and authority state of real EKS/PKS artifacts be represented without losing domain meaning? If yes, investigate further. If no, discard the model.
rows.statement: Proposes the first concrete falsifiable experiment for the complex-number model: test K=S+iA against real EKS/PKS artifacts and discard the model if domain meaning is lost.

rows.anchor: CAPPI's numeric epistemic stack (mu/tau/w -> Bayesian fusion -> quality score) has ZERO current-architecture support. None of EKS/PKS/AIP uses a continuous calibrated confidence signal, a Bayesian fusion step, or a scalar quality score.
rows.statement: Reports the single strongest case in the investigation of an elegant external principle unsupported by current evidence: continuous calibrated confidence, per-instance uncertainty, and a reliability weight (mu/tau/w) are absent from all three baselines, whose discrete verdict vocabularies and honest UNKNOWN answers are philosophically the inverse of a probabilistic quality score.

aliases: Davidson Inquiries into Truth and Interpretation, against the identified gaps

sources.note: A very large (2133-line) extraction from Davidson's Inquiries into Truth and Interpretation (Essays 1-18: Radical Interpretation, Belief and the Basis of Meaning, Thought and Talk, On the Very Idea of a Conceptual Scheme, The Method of Truth in Metaphysics, Communication and Convention), explicitly scoped as NOT covering Davidson's later coherence-theory/externalism essays. Central finding: Davidson's radical-interpretation problem (constructing an interpretation without already knowing the language's meaning or the speaker's beliefs) is structurally the KnowledgeOS problem of constructing semantic knowledge from observation without presupposing the interpretation being established, yielding Observation!=Interpretation, Evidence!=Meaning, Meaning!=Belief, with Meaning/Belief/Truth needing to be reconstructed TOGETHER (an interdependent, not linear, process) -- proposing the semantic layer be modelled as constraint-solving/abductive/holistic, not parsing. Davidson's interpreter (observe->discriminate->hypothesize->assign truth conditions->compare hypotheses->test->maintain coherence->revise) constructs a FINITE GENERATIVE THEORY from which infinitely many interpretations follow, offered as a strong structural analogy for a KnowledgeOS kernel-as-generative-mechanism (script-K -> {K_1,...,K_n}) rather than a stored answer set. Distinguishes TruthConditions from Probability (Truth(c,t) iff Nexus listens on 8081 at t, versus P(c)=0.95 answering a different question), giving TruthConditions -> EpistemicProbability rather than Probability -> Meaning, and reinforcing Pi_t!=K_t. Combines with a 'Freedman' source (not itself read in this batch) into 'no hidden inference layer': every KnowledgeOS determination should be traceable through Observation->Evidence->Interpretation->SemanticRepresentation->Assumptions->Model/Reasoning->CandidateConclusion->Validation->Determination. States Davidsonian holism -- Meaning(k_i) is not independent, but Meaning(k_i)=f(k_i,K_t,Context) -- refining atomic claims as useful-but-not-semantically-isolated (Atomicity != Context-independence, illustrated by 'Nexus server runs RHEL 9.8' vs 'Nexus container runs on RHEL 9.8'). Proposes reconceiving Knowledge Space as a relational structure KS_t=(K_t,R_t) with R_t containing entails/contradicts/presupposes/supports/depends-on/contextualizes/excludes/compatible-with relations, rather than a bare storage set, connecting to the corpus's DDD/evidence-graph work; states knowledge quality depends partly on this relational structure, not merely atomic-claim count. Refines the candidate Buddhi/Discriminate operator to Buddhi_candidate=Discriminate(Interpretations | Evidence,Context,Coherence,Truth), explicitly [INF] not an established Gita-KnowledgeOS identity. Corrects the principle of charity from maximize-agreement to BestInterpretation=argmax(Intelligibility) subject to Truth+Evidence+Coherence+Context, warning against optimizing for consensus over epistemic defensibility; combines with a 'Freedman' rival-hypotheses principle into 'maintain competing interpretations/models until evidence discriminates' (premature collapse is dangerous). Reports Davidson's INDETERMINACY result (multiple significantly different theories can fit all available evidence equally well even once all evidence is in) as grounds for distinguishing epistemic uncertainty (don't know which is correct) from representational indeterminacy (several representations are equally adequate) -- these are not the same. Adds a second independent argument (via the Fahrenheit/Celsius numerical-representation example) for RepresentationEquality(A,B) != SemanticEquivalence(A,B), extending the corpus's existing SNF-based non-collapse; raises the research question 'what is invariant across valid KnowledgeOS representations?' (truth conditions? entailment? causal relations? identity? temporal relations? evidential dependencies? inquiry adequacy? -- each must be tested). Uses Davidson's rejection of radically incommensurable conceptual schemes to argue different representations != different worlds and different ontologies must be compared through shared constraints/evidence, while explicitly NOT claiming Davidson supports one neutral universal KnowledgeOS ontology (he rejects a neutral common coordinate system entirely) -- ontology is constrained by truth/evidence/language/relations, not unified by a common ground. Strengthens 'the Knower owns the frame' into a candidate SemanticFrame=(Agent,Time,Context,Language,Purpose), and extends the Inquiry tuple with a semantic-interpretation-constraints field: Q=(T,P,C,R,Gamma,Sigma), motivated by Davidson's Communication-and-Convention finding that successful communication does not require identical prior languages/interpretation theories (Communication != shared representation; Communication = successful alignment of interpretation), aimed at preventing the AI failure of answering the wrong interpretation of a question. Extracts an anti-premature-definition principle (reduction/definition can be 'too much to expect'; theory-to-evidence fit may be looser than a strict definition) matching the corpus's own discipline against freezing Knowledge:=X too early. CLOSES by proposing a concrete 'KnowledgeOS Kernel Minimality Experiment': a 13-operator candidate set {Observe,Interpret,Represent,Relate,Discriminate,Hypothesize,Infer,DetectGap,Challenge,Validate,Revise,Determine,Select} to be tested one-at-a-time-removed against a checklist of required capabilities, with explicit removal-test logic (if removing Interpret makes semantic knowledge impossible, it survives as primitive; if removing Hypothesize just causes another operator to absorb its function, it may not be primitive; if Zero can be represented as a predicate over K_t rather than an operation, it is not a kernel primitive) -- proposing Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC) be treated as a STATE PREDICATE rather than assumed a primitive kernel operation. Final framing: Freedman says don't trust an unsupported inference; Davidson says don't even assume the interpretation of the evidence is already known -- reframing the central KnowledgeOS question from 'how do we infer knowledge from evidence' to 'how does an epistemic system construct, constrain, validate, and revise the INTERPRETATION through which evidence becomes knowledge.'

rows.anchor: How can we construct an interpretation when we do not already know the meaning of the language or the beliefs of the speaker? ... Meaning, Belief, Truth must be reconstructed together.
rows.statement: Frames Davidson's radical-interpretation problem as structurally identical to a core KnowledgeOS problem: constructing semantic knowledge from observation without presupposing the interpretation being established; yields Observation!=Interpretation, Evidence!=Meaning, Meaning!=Belief, with the key insight that Meaning/Belief/Truth must be reconstructed TOGETHER, not derived linearly.

rows.anchor: A finite generative theory -> many particular determinations. ... the KnowledgeOS kernel is a transformation mechanism rather than merely a knowledge database.
rows.statement: Reports Davidson's interpreter as constructing a finite generative theory from which interpretations of infinitely many utterances follow, offered as strong structural support (independent of Rescorla) for the hypothesis that the KnowledgeOS kernel is a generative transformation mechanism (script-K -> {K_1,...,K_n}) rather than a stored answer database.

rows.anchor: Truth(c,t) iff Nexus listens on port 8081 at t. ... P(c)=0.95 does not tell us what would make c true. TruthConditions != Probability.
rows.statement: Introduces truth conditions as a semantic layer distinct from probability: a claim's truth condition specifies what would make it true, which a probability/confidence value does not supply, reinforcing Pi_t!=K_t and proposing TruthConditions->EpistemicProbability rather than Probability->Meaning.

rows.anchor: Meaning(k_i) not-equiv Meaning(k_i) independently. More plausibly: Meaning(k_i) = f(k_i, K_t, Context). ... Atomicity != Context independence.
rows.statement: Applies Davidsonian holism to the atomic-claim model: an atomic claim's meaning is not semantically isolated but a function of the whole knowledge state and context (Meaning(k_i)=f(k_i,K_t,Context)), illustrated by 'Nexus server runs RHEL 9.8' vs 'Nexus container runs on RHEL 9.8' -- yielding the principle Atomicity != Context-independence.

rows.anchor: KS_t = (K_t, R_t) where R contains relations such as entails, contradicts, presupposes, supports, depends on, contextualizes, excludes, is compatible with. ... Knowledge quality depends partly on relational structure, not merely atomic claim count.
rows.statement: Proposes reconceiving Knowledge Space as a relational structure KS_t=(K_t,R_t) rather than a bare storage set, with R_t carrying entailment/contradiction/presupposition/support/dependency/contextualization/exclusion/compatibility relations among claims -- explicitly a research candidate, not the KnowledgeOS definition, connected to the corpus's existing DDD/evidence-graph work.

rows.anchor: Buddhi_candidate = Discriminate(Interpretations | Evidence, Context, Coherence, Truth).
rows.statement: Refines the candidate Buddhi/Discriminate operator using Davidsonian interpretation constraints (coherence, truth conditions, evidence, background beliefs, behavioral compatibility) into Buddhi_candidate=Discriminate(Interpretations | Evidence,Context,Coherence,Truth), explicitly [INF] not an established Gita-KnowledgeOS identity.

rows.anchor: BestInterpretation = argmax Intelligibility, subject to Truth+Evidence+Coherence+Context. ... otherwise KnowledgeOS could optimize for what everybody agrees with rather than what is epistemically defensible.
rows.statement: Corrects a naive principle-of-charity formulation (BestInterpretation=argmax Agreement) to BestInterpretation=argmax Intelligibility subject to Truth+Evidence+Coherence+Context, explicitly to prevent KnowledgeOS from optimizing for consensus rather than epistemic defensibility.

rows.anchor: Maintain competing interpretations/models until evidence discriminates. ... premature collapse is dangerous.
rows.statement: Combines Davidson's requirement to compare multiple candidate interpretations with a parallel rival-hypotheses principle into a generalized rule: maintain competing interpretations/models simultaneously until evidence actually discriminates between them, warning that the corpus already shows a tendency toward proliferating candidate models without ever selecting one, but that premature collapse is equally dangerous.

rows.anchor: significantly different theories may still fit the evidence equally well [after all evidence is available]. ... Evidence sufficient for adequacy does not imply unique representation.
rows.statement: Reports Davidson's indeterminacy-of-interpretation result (multiple significantly different theories can fit all available evidence equally well) as grounds for a KnowledgeOS distinction between epistemic uncertainty (we don't know which is correct) and representational indeterminacy (several representations are equally adequate) -- explicitly not the same phenomenon, and both compatible with Evidence-sufficient-for-adequacy not implying a unique representation.

rows.anchor: Fahrenheit and Celsius differ numerically while preserving the relevant structure. ... RepresentationEquality(A,B) should be defined independently from SemanticEquivalence(A,B).
rows.statement: Uses Davidson's temperature-scale example (Fahrenheit and Celsius numerically differ while preserving the same relational/semantic pattern) as a second, independent argument for separating RepresentationEquality(A,B) from SemanticEquivalence(A,B), extending the corpus's existing SNF(x)=SNF(y) does not imply x=y non-collapse with a positive converse case (different representations, same meaning).

rows.anchor: What is invariant across valid KnowledgeOS representations? Possibilities include: truth conditions, entailment relations, causal relations, identity, temporal relations, evidential dependencies, inquiry adequacy. But we must test each.
rows.statement: Poses, drawing on Davidson's claim that meaning may be what remains invariant across alternative acceptable truth theories, the research question of what is invariant across valid KnowledgeOS representations, listing seven untested candidate invariants (truth conditions, entailment, causal relations, identity, temporal relations, evidential dependencies, inquiry adequacy), framed as potentially more important than finding one canonical representation.

rows.anchor: Different representations != different worlds. ... Ontology is constrained by truth, evidence, language, and relations [but there is no neutral common coordinate system].
rows.statement: Reports Davidson's rejection of radically incommensurable conceptual schemes (different representations != different worlds; different ontologies must be compared via shared constraints/evidence) while equally explicitly rejecting the opposite overreading that Davidson licenses one neutral universal KnowledgeOS ontology -- Davidson denies a neutral common coordinate system entirely, so ontology remains constrained rather than unified.

rows.anchor: SemanticFrame = (Agent, Time, Context, Language, Purpose). ... a claim cannot always be interpreted without knowing whose claim, under what conditions, for what purpose.
rows.statement: Strengthens the 'Knower owns the frame' principle into a candidate SemanticFrame=(Agent,Time,Context,Language,Purpose), grounded in Davidson's finding that interpreting an utterance requires accounting for speaker, time, circumstances, beliefs, intentions and actions.

rows.anchor: Communication != shared representation. Communication = Successful alignment of interpretation. ... Inquiry + Semantic Contract. Q=(T,P,C,R,Gamma,Sigma).
rows.statement: Extends the Inquiry tuple with a semantic-interpretation-constraints field, Q=(T,P,C,R,Gamma,Sigma), motivated by Davidson's Communication-and-Convention argument that successful communication does not require speaker and hearer to share identical languages or prior interpretation theories (Communication != shared representation; Communication = successful alignment of interpretation) -- aimed at preventing KnowledgeOS from answering the wrong interpretation of a client's question.

rows.anchor: reduction and definition are sometimes too much to expect; the relation between theory and evidence may be looser. ... Theory -> constraints -> empirical consequences -> increasing determination.
rows.statement: Extracts an anti-premature-definition principle from Davidson (definitional reduction can be too much to expect of a theory; theory-evidence fit may be looser than strict definition), matching and reinforcing the corpus's own discipline against prematurely fixing 'Knowledge := X.'
